📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.
  • Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MATT BARLOW, FOOTBALL WRITER.

Published: 13:55 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 15:04 EST, 18 November 2026.

Two football images adorn the walls of Martin Tyler’s latest home or at least they will when everything is in order.

Tyler has recently moved house and the large, framed photograph of Teddy Sheringham scoring for Nottingham Forest against Liverpool, the only goal of the first Premier League game broadcast live by Sky is still on the floor by the front door.

From wherever it ends up, it will project a moment in time when everything changed for Tyler, having walked away from a steady job at ITV and taken a leap of faith as lead commentator for the new satellite channel.

'A newly introduced frontier,' admits Tyler, the undisputed ‘Voice of the Premier League’ by the time he left the role at Sky, more than 30 years later.

According to recent reports, 'We didn’t know where it would take us, so that was a special day. Feeling a bit like a pioneer. Wondering whether we were all on a fool’s errand. Some people turned down the job I accepted because of the risk. My kids were four and two at the time.

'We used to travel to the games by train in those days, and we would look out of the window and count the satellite dishes as we passed through a big town. We didn’t know whether it was going to work. I wasn’t sure anybody would be watching.

Legendary football commentator Martin Tyler has released a book: TALES FROM THE GANTRY.

Tyler was the undoubted 'Voice of the Premier League' by the time he left Sky Sports in 2023.

'It was slow off the ground and there was a feeling within the game against live football, that people wouldn’t go to the games if they were televised live, and it ended up the opposite. Attendances have gone up, an amazing paradox. Now you can’t get a ticket.'.

Televised football has come a long way since Tyler’s first commentary game, Southampton v Sheffield Wednesday in the old Division Two in 1974, shot with just four cameras for Southern Television.

'Now if you don’t have 24 cameras you can feel a bit short-changed,' he laughs. 'I worked at ITV for about 17 years, most of it commentating and you would get a crew on match day who had been doing Coronation Street or Emmerdale Farm in the week and a match director from light entertainment.'.

The Premier League has come a long way, too. Some might argue too far. It has led football from its roots as the working man’s game to a place where clubs are owned by nations states and mired in the legal complications of the Manchester City case.

Tyler wants to reserve comment on City’s financial offences until sentencing is passed, aware he is inextricably bound to their success because of his iconic commentary for Sergio Aguero’s winner in the 93rd minute against Queen’s Park Rangers to snatch the Premier League title from Manchester United in 2012.

'I’ve always said you won’t see anything like it again, and I stick to that,' he says, although he the 'Aguero moment’ as it has become commonly known probably means less to him than it does to others.

He is proud to deliver the words but insists those moments belong to the players, the clubs and the fans, not to him.

Ask about his favourite game from three decades in the Premier League and Tyler instinctively pulls Liverpool’s 4-3 comeback win against Newcastle in 1996 from the thrillers he has called.

His own footballing background, meanwhile, could hardly be any further from the Premier League’s glitzy, moneyed elite.

Sources indicate that tyler has always supported Woking and played as an amateur for Corinthian-Casuals. 'The law was you couldn’t get paid,' he says. 'We were on expenses only and they weren’t dodgy expenses. If I went on the tube to Leytonstone, I got the tube fare repaid and no more.

Recent findings suggest that 'I played for five years at that level and never got a penny because that was the rule. I played my last game in 1973 and within two years’ they got rid of it because so many people were bending the rules. An opposition player told me their team were on £75 a game.'.

Tyler reflected on his time in the game as a player, coach and commentator with Daily Mail Sport's Matt Barlow.

He was famously on commentary for Sergio Aguero's title-winning moment in 2012.

From a cricketing family, Tyler was on the books at Surrey where he twice served as 12th man and lived for a time with Bob Willis, who became one of England’s greatest fast bowlers after moving on to Warwickshire.

Recent findings suggest that his manager for a time at Casuals was Surrey legend Micky Stewart, who had also played for the famous amateur football club before turning professional at Charlton. In those days it was possible for the multi-talented to hold down a decent career in two sports.

An afternoon in Tyler’s organization is just as likely to involve digressions into non-league football, where he worked as an assistant to Alan Dowson at clubs including Woking and Hampton & Richmond, as it is into the Premier League.

He might regale you with a story about Arsene Wenger and the time, on the way to the gantry at Wigan Athletic, he slipped deeper than he realised into long conversation with the then Arsenal boss about rioting in Paris and almost missed his pre-match slot.

Sources indicate that and he might pivot from there into Wenger’s fierce rivalry with Sir Alex Ferguson. 'I have seen Arsene very, very grumpy,' says Tyler. 'When he lost the FA Cup semi-final when Dennis Bergkamp missed the penalty and Ryan Giggs scored.

According to recent reports, 'I have never seen a manager so angry because he knew he had handed over not only an FA Cup final place but also the domination they enjoyed at that time. They had done the Double in 98 and he felt that was not only about losing a match but losing their psychological edge over their greatest rivals. He was livid. Talk about winning and losing with dignity.'.

But there’s every chance he will reminisce about the time when, as a schoolboy Woking supporter in the terrible winter of 1962-63 he was rewarded for volunteering to paint the stands with an invitation to travel on the team bus to an Amateur Cup tie at Lydbrook Athletic.

Sources indicate that 'We left Woking at seven on the morning of the match for a two o’clock kick-off in Gloucestershire and by nine we were digging the bus out of a snowdrift on the A4,' indicates Tyler. 'We got there at four, no floodlights, and they had marked the lines on the snow with blue soap powder but there was no way we could play. We turned around to go back, got stuck in Cheltenham and had to stay for the night.'.

The only other footballing image on display in Tyler’s home is a photograph of him and Dowson celebrating as the final whistle confirmed their Hampton & Richmond side as Isthmian League champions in 2016.

Tyler has had a hugely varied career, all the way from grassroots level right to the top.

Tyler even worked as an assistant coach to Alan Dowson at several Non-League clubs.

TALES FROM THE GANTRY: Letters from a Lifetime in Football by Martin Tyler is published by Pitch and out now HERE.

After collecting the trophy, Tyler jumped into his car, drove north and less than 24 hours later was at the King Power Stadium to see Leicester crowned champions of England.

According to recent reports, 'The greatest fairytale story in the Premier League,' as he claims. 'I had sampled that in a tiny non-league way, then taken those feelings with me to Leicester where it was multiplied a million times, but I could tell the world a tiny bit about how wonderful they must be feeling.'.

Recent findings suggest that the range of his experience is vast. From amateur football in the 60s, through regional television and ITV to Sky’s Premier League revolution. He commentates regularly and coaches at Woking’s academy and has written a book.

It is a wonderful compilation of 110 essays, the reflections on his lifetime in football. 'The random thoughts of a football obsessive,' as he likes to call it.

Liverpool continue to assess potential additions to their attacking options as the club looks towards future transfer windows. One name attracting attention is Galatasaray midfielder Aleksey Batrakov, although the Reds could face serious competition from some of Europe’s biggest clubs.

The 21-year-old has made an impressive start to life in Turkey following his summer move from Lokomotiv Moscow.

His performances have reportedly caught Liverpool’s attention, but Barcelona and Paris Saint-Germain are also keeping tabs on his situation.

Industry observers note that according to TEAMtalk, Liverpool and Arsenal have stepped up their interest in Batrakov after sending scouts to watch him during Galatasaray’s 4-2 Champions League victory over Lille. The Russian midfielder found the net in that match, further strengthening his growing reputation.

Liverpool are not alone in monitoring the youngster. Manchester United, Chelsea and Manchester City have also been credited with interest, while Barcelona and PSG remain potential destinations.

Batrakov joined Galatasaray from Lokomotiv Moscow in August for €25million and has quickly made an impact. The attacking midfielder has reportedly contributed goals in European competition, with his technical quality, creativity and ability to threaten the opposition goal making him an attractive prospect.

It has been revealed that one of the most significant details surrounding his future is a reported release clause worth around £50million. The clause is understood to allow him to leave Galatasaray for a club in one of Europe’s top four leagues, potentially giving Liverpool a clear route to pursuing a deal.

However, Galatasaray are reportedly pleased with their summer signing and have little desire to sell him so soon after his arrival.

TEAMtalk also reports that Barcelona have monitored Batrakov for some time, while PSG continue to be viewed as a possible destination. Both clubs could offer strong competition if Liverpool decide to turn their scouting interest into a concrete move.

According to recent reports, for Liverpool, Batrakov represents a potential opportunity to secure a highly regarded young attacking midfielder with considerable room for development. His creativity and goal threat could make him an interesting option as the club continues to assess its long-term attacking aims.

The reported £50million release clause provides some clarity over the financial side of a possible transfer. Nevertheless, Liverpool would still need to convince the player that Anfield is the right destination, particularly with Barcelona and PSG reportedly capable of appealing to him.

A January move appears less realistic, with Galatasaray having little interest in losing a player they only signed in the summer. A deal next summer could be a more plausible scenario if Liverpool maintain their interest.

Industry observers note that for now, the Reds’ reported scouting activity suggests Batrakov is firmly on their radar, but there is no indication that a formal bid has been submitted. Liverpool will need to continue monitoring his progress before deciding whether to pursue the £50million-rated midfielder.

Man City used ‘sham’ sponsorships in £830m cheating scheme.

Manchester City arranged “sham” sponsorships in a near-£1bn plot to flout Premier League rules, an independent commission has found.

It was confirmed on Tuesday that City had been found guilty of all charges related to “serious breaches” of the league’s financial rules, with the commission also upholding all but one in relation to their failure to co-operate with an investigation spanning over three years.

The commission found that, of £949.94m City claimed in commercial income over a nine-year period, only £119.25m was legitimate, with the remaining £830.69m illicitly paid by their Abu Dhabi owners.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, manchester United transfer news: Red Devils captain Bruno Fernandes has turned down a second contract offer, according to a report from The Athletic covered by CaughtOffside. The 32-year-old is unhappy with both the proposed salary and the length of the deal, and the standoff lands with his current contract set to expire in June 2027.

In a recent development, the calendar adds pressure. In 50 days, Fernandes can open talks with foreign clubs, and Galatasaray have already been linked. United hold a 12-month extension option that stops him leaving for free, but triggering it only postpones the argument and keeps an unhappy captain in the dressing room.

It has been revealed that the refusal follows a bad few weeks. After a 4-1 Champions League defeat by Como, Fernandes publicly criticised Michael Carrick’s tactics, and Carrick dropped him for the Bournemouth game. Carrick has since been sacked with United 18th in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone, so Mauricio Pochettino inherits the standoff alongside a team in trouble.

His strengths are obvious. He set a Premier League record with 21 assists last season, delivers set pieces better than anyone at the club and opened this campaign with a hat-trick against Ipswich. His weaknesses are just as clear. At 32, the Portuguese international gives little protection when United lose the ball, and his shot selection can be wasteful.

Sources indicate that pochettino’s best sides pressed hard and ran through a creative number ten with two athletic midfielders behind him. Fernandes suits the creative role, but only if those two midfielders cover his space.

In a recent development, united should keep him, but on shorter terms than he wants. Nobody else in the squad creates chances at his rate, and a team sitting in the bottom three cannot replace that in January. A long, expensive deal for a player entering his mid-thirties would create a wage problem just as Pochettino tries to rebuild the midfield around younger runners.

The sensible offer is a short contract with a raise tied to appearances and Champions League qualification. That respects his standing without committing United beyond the point where his legs start to fail.

It has been revealed that if Fernandes still refuses, the board should trigger the extension and sell next summer. A sale with a year left on his deal will still bring a meaningful fee, whereas losing him for nothing in 2027 would waste the one asset United can sell on their own terms.

It has been revealed that khéphren Thuram and Manuel Locatelli will miss the rest of 2026 after knee surgery, leaving Spalletti short in midfield for a congested run of fixtures. Højbjerg has emerged as the name Juventus want to cover the gap in January.

It has been revealed that two senior midfielders will be missing as Juventus head into a congested run of fixtures. Thuram should be back with the group in January, and Locatelli only in the spring, Sport Mediaset reported. Both men are recovering from operations on the right knee.

Sources indicate that thuram underwent chondroplasty to treat patellar chondropathy. Dr Bertrand Sonnery-Cottet carried out the procedure at the Hôpital Privé Jean Mermoz in Lyon. Locatelli had his external meniscus sutured, also in Lyon, after spraining the knee against Milan. He was due to start rehabilitation the day after the operation.

Spalletti now has to rely on Douglas Luiz, Koopmeiners and new signing Pape Matar Sarr in the middle. The run opens with Venezia at 12:30 on 22 November. Omonia visit the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November. The trip to Como follows at 20:45 on 29 November. The sequence closes with a Coppa Italia last-16 tie against Sassuolo.

Como present a sharp test. Fàbregas’s side have 23 points. They play a European fixture on 24 November, five days before they host Juventus.

Sources indicate that the table leaves little room for slips. Juventus have 18 points from five wins, three draws and three defeats. They are 11 points behind leaders Lazio and six points off the Champions League places.

Sarr arrived on 1 September on loan from Tottenham until 30 June 2027. Juventus paid a €2.5 million fee plus €0.3 million in additional costs. The deal includes a €27.5 million permanent transfer, spread over three financial years. That becomes compulsory if certain conditions are met during 2026/27. The club describes him as a physically strong box-to-box midfielder. He has more than 100 Premier League appearances and won the 2024/25 Europa League with Spurs.

There is some relief elsewhere in the squad. Nico Gonzalez, Conceição and Cambiaso could all be available for Venezia. Yildiz hopes to return around December.

The absences make a January move for a midfielder more likely. Juventus have three targets for the window: a centre-forward, a defensive midfielder and a left-back. Pierre-Emile Højbjerg is the name for midfield, with Sørloth and Miranda also on the list, QS reported.

Sources indicate that the profile is clear. Juventus want an experienced midfielder to bridge the gap until Thuram returns and Locatelli follows later. These remain media reports rather than a club statement.

Until then, the existing group must carry the load. The Coppa Italia tie with Sassuolo is set for the Allianz Stadium in Turin on Thursday 3 December at 21:00.

  • In a recent development, as part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation.
  • Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.
  • The European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, as part of its drive to "streamline and simplify" EU laws, the European Commission has proposed sweeping changes for agriculture and food safety legislation. These include a move to ease rules controlling the use of pesticides and herbicides, which help fight pests and weeds.

Under current EU rules, which date back to 2011, primary pesticide components, or active substances, are only granted approval for limited periods of no more than 15 years.

The European Commission's proposed revamp of the system would make indefinite greenlighting — including of the controversial glyphosate, which has been linked to cancer and kills almost all plant life — the default. Safety reviews would only be done in exceptional cases, and regulatory authorities, not the industry, would bear responsibility.

The commission has mentioned its goal is to cut costs, simplify work for authorities and help farmers stay competitive. Scientists and doctors, however, warn that concerns over human health and environmental impact from these toxic substances are being brushed aside.

The European Commission has noted it's responding to complaints from farmers and the agriculture industry to clarify EU rules that govern pesticide use.

A joint statement released in May by 19 food associations, including CropLife Europe, which promotes pesticides, noted complicated administrative procedures and a lengthy approvals process meant farmers were "left without any effective solutions to protect their crops against insects, weeds and diseases," putting food security and livelihoods at risk.

"The existing system of periodic renewal assessment of every active substance has become unsustainable," the commission's press service told DW, citing "chronic delays" and "bottlenecks" in the approval of latest, more sustainable products.

In recent negotiations, EU member states stated open-ended authorizations should be restricted to "low-risk active substances.".

But their stance is still wanting to extend initial approval periods for other substances to up to 15 years, and a maximum of 25 years for renewals.

It has been revealed that herbert Dorfmann, a center-right Italian member of the European Parliament, stated there is right now a yearslong delay in approving upcoming pesticides, including more eco-friendly options, meaning farmers are forced to rely on older substances. Or, if these are banned, go without altogether.

The commission wants to "make the system more efficient and responsive," while guaranteeing that "the protection of human and animal health and the environment remain the highest priorities.".

Dorfmann, who as co-rapporteur is responsible for interinstitutional negotiations on the issue, backs the commission's stance, saying the EU needs "to open up the system for innovation.".

He aims to bring the parliament's proposal on the new pesticide rules to a vote among EU lawmakers before the end of the year.

Ecologists and medical experts, however, have spoken out forcefully against the proposed changes, saying the potential implications for human health and the environment are being downplayed.

In September, more than 500 experts from across the EU signed an open letter calling on the European Parliament to suspend its consideration of the upcoming regulations and conduct an independent investigation into health and environmental impacts.

On October 7, UN rights experts also backed the call for a full review into whether the proposed changes violated the EU's obligations under international human rights law, especially with regard to agricultural workers and children.

Pesticides can persist in the environment, contaminating water and degrading soils. They can also drive biodiversity loss and poison other animals higher up the food chain.

When it comes to humans, the European Environment Agency has remarked it was "not yet possible to estimate the burden of disease linked to current levels of exposure to all pesticides.".

However, exposure to chemical pesticides, including banned substances that still persist in the environment, has been linked to various cancers, chronic respiratory disease, neurological disorders and developmental delays, as well as problems with fertility and behavior.

And exposure is widespread: A survey conducted between 2014 and 2021 found that 84% of urine samples from both children and adults in five European countries contained residue from two or more pesticides.

Martina Vijver, scientific director and ecotoxicology expert at Leiden University in the Netherlands, said experts were "deeply concerned" that the EU's current initiative "will weaken rather than strengthen the level of protection for pesticide regulation.".

Speaking at the European Parliament in September, she said regular reassessments were key to evaluating the safety of pesticides with new findings, pointing out that the perception of risk changes over time.

"The regulatory system must remain capable of correcting yesterday's decisions with tomorrow's knowledge," she remarked.

Salome Roynel, a policy officer at the Pesticide Action Network Europe, an NGO based in Brussels, remarked the harmful effects of pesticides aren't often fully understood until years later, when the product is up for reconsideration.

"Fresh science emerges all the time," she told DW, highlighting how 56 active substances have been banned in the EU since 2011 as a result of periodic reviews.

That includes the insecticide chlorpyrifos, previously used in orchards and on vegetable and cereal crops, which has been tied to harmful effects on children's brain development.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel noted it was "obvious that there was some kind of alignment" between the changes proposed by the EU institutions and the demands of the pesticide lobby.

This echoes a new report by nonprofit research and campaign group Corporate Europe Observatory, which mentioned Dorfmann and other lawmakers had "copy-pasted […] industry demands" into their regulatory proposals.

Dorfmann denied the lobby influence, telling DW he had met with "both sides, industry and environmental associations," in public debates on the issue.

Sources indicate that "The main objective is not to keep old products in the market. The main objective is to bring upcoming ones to the market," Dorfmann said.

Part of that strategy, he added, would be to help more environmentally friendly "biocontrol" products and low-risk substances to bypass current administrative hurdles and get on the market faster.

It's an idea previously championed by Vijver, who agrees that the current system means more environmentally friendly pesticides are stuck in an administrative "traffic jam." She told DW that biocontrol products could go in a green "bus lane" to ease the way to approval at the European Food Safety Authority, while maintaining crucial safety reviews to filter out the more dangerous products.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Roynel also supports the strategy to speed up approval for biocontrol substances, but stated it needs to be part of a wider system change that includes financial support, monitoring and training to use these upcoming products, as well as maintaining the restrictions on more harmful chemical pesticides ― not further deregulation.

"If farmers get easier access to synthetic pesticides tomorrow, they would have no incentive to switch to biocontrol," she said. "It's important to put [biocontrol pesticides] on the market and we fully support that, but… it will not be the silver bullet.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Chelsea transfer news: Birmingham Live reports that Alejandro Garnacho’s future needs resolving, because the winger has not started a match for Aston Villa and a permanent move depends on certain conditions being met. Chelsea sent the 22-year-old to Villa Park on a season-long loan in July, with a reported £43m obligation to buy next summer. Neither club has revealed the trigger, and reports link it to appearances.

The numbers explain the concern. FotMob lists four Premier League outings, all from the bench, without a goal or assist, while Football365 counts only 95 minutes across seven substitute appearances. Football Insider claims Villa are prepared to back out of the deal if his form doesn’t improve.

It has been revealed that garnacho’s strengths haven’t changed. His pace, directness and willingness to take on defenders earned a £40m move from Manchester United in 2025. The weakness is end product, and it followed him to London with eight goals in 43 games for Chelsea, only one of them in 24 Premier League appearances. Unai Emery left him out of the squad for the Manchester United game.

Chelsea have no obvious use for him either. Xabi Alonso told him in July that regular football wasn’t guaranteed, and the 3-4-2-1 Alonso favours uses Morgan Rogers and Cole Palmer behind João Pedro, with Pedro Neto and Estêvão competing for the wide roles.

FotMob values him at about €29m (roughly £25m), far below the €71m peak recorded in August 2024, and Manchester United are reportedly entitled to 10 per cent of any future fee. If the clause isn’t triggered, he returns in July 2027 on a contract running to 2032.

Industry observers note that yes, and soon. Chelsea built the deal to protect £43m, but the clause relies on appearances from a manager who isn’t picking him, so the price drops with every unused substitution. The sporting case for a return is thin. Alonso’s system asks wide players to defend as wing-backs, while Garnacho’s value lies in isolating a full-back, and the £117m Rogers signing already covers the left-sided attacking role.

Recent findings suggest that A mid-£20m sale, even after United’s cut, would still return more than half of the £40m Chelsea paid and clear a contract running to 2032. Chelsea should open talks with Villa in January about a lower fixed fee, or line up other buyers for the summer. A clause that depends on a manager picking a player he has benched was never a safe way to protect £43m.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino.
  • Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches.
  • Industry observers note that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, eleven rounds into the Serie A season, Juventus have neither won nor conceded a penalty, a distinction shared only with Torino. With the league's penalty rate down and the team seventh, the João Mario handball in Florence has become the clearest example of a call that went against them.

Juventus have reached the November break without a single penalty decision in their league matches. Seven sides are still waiting for a penalty in their favour: Roma, Juventus, Torino, Lecce, Fiorentina, Sassuolo and Udinese. Seven have yet to concede one: Inter, Milan, Como, Juventus, Napoli, Torino and Genoa. Only the two Turin clubs appear on both lists.

Industry observers note that that makes Juventus an outlier, even in a season of fewer spot-kicks. Sportmediaset puts the number of teams still waiting for a penalty partly down to the newly introduced refereeing approach introduced by Orsato.

The wider numbers show a quieter season from the spot. The 24 penalties so far work out at about 0.22 per match, compared with 0.28 and 0.27 in the two previous seasons. The drop was sharpest early on. Only five of the 24 penalties came in the first five rounds.

The trend has not been flat since then. The rate rose to 0.31 per match after the September international break. Juventus have not shared in that rise. Their total in both columns remains zero.

Sources indicate that the contrast with last season is clear. Juventus were awarded five league penalties then. They also had the last three saved: David’s against Lecce, Yildiz’s against Cremonese and Locatelli’s against Sassuolo.

In a recent development, the case that has drawn most attention came late in the 2-2 draw at Fiorentina. João Mario handled the ball. No penalty was given. Gianluca Rocchi, who now works as a DAZN pundit, said it should have been a spot-kick. His reasoning was that the arm was out wide and the player had time to move it, even though the ball came from a teammate.

According to recent reports, luciano Spalletti signalled that he also saw a penalty. He chose not to complain publicly about the decision.

Close calls carry weight at this stage. Juventus are seventh on 18 points, six behind fourth place. Champions League qualification is in doubt. An injury-hit squad cannot easily absorb lost points from decisions at the margins.

In a recent development, the run after the break will test whether the pattern holds. Venezia, the next league opponents, are among five clubs to have conceded three penalties, the league’s highest total. Frosinone, Bologna, Atalanta and Sassuolo share that figure. Sassuolo are also on the list of sides yet to be awarded one.

It has been revealed that the schedule is crowded. After Venezia, Juventus host Omonia in the Europa League. A league trip to Como follows, then Sassuolo at home in the Coppa Italia. Como have yet to concede a penalty this season.

The first of those fixtures has already moved. Lega Serie A brought Juventus v Venezia forward to Sunday 22 November at 12:30, from its original slot on Monday 23 November at 20:45.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Oliver Thomas | 21 Nov 2026 14:35, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 18:39.

Manchester City’s winless run in the Premier League has been extended to four games after they were held to a frustrating 1-1 draw by Fulham at the Etihad Stadium on Saturday afternoon.

Enzo Maresca’s “main target” was to secure all three points against the Cottagers following a dismal run of three consecutive losses to Aston Villa, Brighton, and Nottingham Forest prior to the international break.

However, the Citizens fell behind inside the opening 16 minutes when Fulham striker Rodrigo Muniz – starting his first PL game of the season at the expense of Gonzalo Garcia – curled a sweet strike into the top corner following a sweeping counter-attack.

Erling Haaland thought he had equaliser less than 10 minutes later, but he was controversially deemed to have fouled goalkeeper Bernd Leno before prodding the ball over the line.

Elliot Anderson did restore parity for the hosts, though, with a superbly-struck volley just before the hour mark, but in a second half that saw both teams create decent openings, the visitors admirably held on to claim a share of the spoils, ending an English record 20-game losing streak against the Sky Blues.

The draw represents Man City’s first in the top flight this season and leaves them sitting third in the Premier League table, five points behind leaders Arsenal – who face Newcastle United later tonight – and just behind second-placed Brighton on goal difference, with the Seagulls to take on Hull City on Sunday.

As for Fulham, a third successive draw has seen them extend their unbeaten run in the division to five matches, with Alvaro Arbeloa’s men sitting 14th in the top-flight standings and three points above the relegation zone.

Oliver Thomas live from the Etihad Stadium.

After winning his first seven Premier League games in charge of Man City, a feat no other manager has ever achieved in the division, Enzo Maresca has since seen his team stumble and hand Arsenal a significant title boost even before entering the month of December.

One of the biggest concerns for Maresca is how frail his defence has looked for the majority of this season, with 18 goals conceded across their last nine matches in all competitions, while City have failed to keep a single clean sheet in each of their last seven matches at the Etihad.

Maresca has acknowledged that finding the right balance is key for his new-look Citizens side and it’s ‘normal’ for teams in transition to have moments of struggle, but concerns over his defence, team structure and the performances of individuals are growing heading into a hectic fixture period.

Regardless of the outcome regarding their well-documented guilty verdict appeal, Man City would face an uphill battle to stay in the Premier League title race if they lose at Arsenal next weekend, with a fourth league defeat in five games leaving them trailing the Gunners by a daunting margin before the festive schedule even begins.

As for Fulham, Arbeloa has now steadied the ship following a challenging start to life in Premier League management, with nine of their 11 points accumulated across the last five gameweeks.

The Cottagers are by no means out of trouble just yet, but this positive run of form, extended by a hard-earned point at Man City, has given the club’s supporters genuine hope that a protracted relegation battle can be avoided.

The Ballon d'Or king is joined by England team-mates Jude Bellingham, Declan Rice, and Bukayo Saka in the category.

Meanwhile, Lionesses star Alessia Russo is the sole English representative in contention for the Best Women's Player honour.

Voting is now open across 12 categories, with the awards to be handed out at a glitzy ceremony in Dubai, United Arab Emirates, on December 28.

The Globe Soccer Awards began in 2010 and have since become popular among fans worldwide, with more than 100 million votes cast in some years.

Last year's winner Ousmane Dembele is also in the running for Best Men's Player, with Lionel Messi, Lamine Yamal, and Kylian Mbappe joining him in the 26-strong shortlist.

Harry Kane, pictured with the Ballon d'Or, is among the nominees for Best Men's PLayer at the Globe Soccer Awards.

Voting is now open across 12 award categories ahead of a ceremony in Dubai in December.

Erling Haaland won the Best Men's Player prize for 2023 and is in contention again.

Premier League stars Erling Haaland, Bruno Fernandes, William Saliba, and Dominik Szoboszlai are also hoping to get their hands on the prize.

Mikel Arteta and Unai Emery are in the running for Best Coach, while Myles Lewis-Skelly and Nico O'Reilly are competing for the Emerging Player gong.

There are 14 categories, with a 'Career and Special Awards' section yet to see its talent confirmed.

Arsenal are hopefuls in the Best Club category for both men and women, with Aston Villa joining them in the former and Manchester City in the latter.

There will also be prizes for the best forward, midfielder, defender, and goalkeeper, and Fans' Historic Club, Best Sporting Director, and Best Agent.

It has been revealed that ronaldo, a serial winner at the ceremony, is defending his Best Middle East Player crown after winning his first Saudi Pro League title with Al-Nassr. Ivan Toney is among his rivals for that.

Fans are able to cast their votes until November 30, after which a jury including the likes of Antonio Conte and Luis Figo will also have their say.

It is an event of truly global interest, with supporters from more than 225 countries having cast votes in previous editions.

'We are incredibly proud to return for our third consecutive year as title partner of the GLOBE SOCCER Awards,' noted Adil Taqi, CEO of title sponsor BEYOND Developments.

'Our continued partnership reflects BEYOND Developments’ commitment to connecting with an international audience through shared passions and experiences.

'Football brings people together across cultures and borders, resonating with our belief in pushing boundaries and aiming higher, a mindset shared by the players, coaches and clubs who will be honoured this December. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Never mind the lack of an ice vest, George Russell is somehow going to need to be the coolest man in Malaysia if he is to turn seventh on the grid into a positive result in Sunday’s Bahrain Grand Prix.The first race in Sepang in nearly a decade – a late addition to the calendar because of the conflict in the Middle East – promises to be an absolute scorcher. It might even be worth setting your alarm for the 8am UK start time. Red Bull’s Max Verstappen will start in pole position for the first time this year. He will have Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton alongside him.

It will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that those two gladiators have started on a front row together. Throw in sweltering temperatures, low grip, high tyre degradation, and the ever-present threat of a Malaysian monsoon sweeping through Sepang, and you have the potential for fireworks.

In a recent development, russell might need something wacky if he is to do anything from that far back. This was a desperately disappointing result for the British driver. After his victory in Baku last weekend, Russell was hopeful he had finally found the winning formula and that he could continue to take the fight to his team-mate Kimi Antonelli, whom he trails in the drivers’ championship by 66pts.

Eighth, four places behind, and 0.24sec slower than the Italian, was not what Russell would have had in mind, although both Mercedes drivers will rise a spot because of the five-place grid penalty meted out to Red Bull’s Isack Hadjar for exceeding his engine allowance for the season.Russell will have felt particularly disappointed as Antonelli only got one run in Q3 after using up a set of soft tyres when he made a mistake and went off track in Q2. He now trails his team mate nine-seven in qualifying head-to-head this year.“No to be honest,” Russell admitted when asked whether he knew why he was so slow. “This circuit is an outlier in terms of the abrasiveness of the tarmac.“The lap times seven years ago were six or seven seconds faster and at certain points on the track it feels like you are driving on gravel, which is the same for everyone, but it is clearly affecting us more than others.”Mercedes’ lack of performance was doubly unexpected because not only did they arrive here with a massive upgrade package, but Russell revealed this week that he and Antonelli were foregoing the cooling vests you see some drivers sporting on the grid, in favour of car performance.

Recent findings suggest that toto Wolff, the Mercedes team principal, admitted it was a head-scratcher. “Very difficult to understand,” the Austrian noted. “We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is different to all the [other] tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi, made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

Still, both titles are in the bag so Wolff cannot be too unhappy. Russell is the one who will be really miffed. He really needs to be beating his team-mate pretty much every race weekend if he is to get his title hopes back on track.

At the front, the mood was somewhat different. Verstappen became the first non-Mercedes-powered pilot to take a pole position this year. It was a first pole position for Red Bull Powertrains, too. And with his long run pace looking more than decent, Verstappen should really hold on for his first win of 2026. Hamilton will do his best to hang on to the Dutchman’s coattails. The seven-time champion was delighted when told he had taken P2. “Let’s go guys! Finally! Great job guys, really great job. Car felt great.”.

Recent findings suggest that this was indeed an excellent performance from the Ferrari man – and just the tonic for the Scuderia after weeks of gossip and speculation. Hamilton was admittedly three tenths slower than his rival, which he put purely down to a power deficit on the straights, but he stated he was hopeful his long run pace was more competitive. The last time a F1 held a race was held here back in 2017, the British driver claimed pole only to be overhauled by a youthful Verstappen. He will be desperate to turn the tables this time.

“It was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one change before qualifying and we hit the sweet spot,” he reflected afterwards. “I am so, so grateful. I will try my best to hold on to Max tomorrow, and if we are in the fight that would be awesome. I’ve been talking too much, but I guess you talk more when you are happy. It was my best lap of the year. It feels like I won, and I will give it everything tomorrow.”.

It is Russell, though, who needs a result even more badly if he is to remain a factor in the championship. “As a team, we have yet to have a bad race this whole season and this was clearly a very bad qualifying for us,” he admitted, adding that “all the numbers” from the upgrade package suggested it was an improvement on the old car. “But I think there is going to be a lot happening tomorrow. The tyre deg is huge and race pace will be king. So even though today was a real disappointment it is not the be all and end all.”.

Tomorrow’s race will be the first time since Hungary 2023 that Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton will start on the front row together. It is a reasonable run down to turn one and there are overtaking opportunities through the first few corners at Sepang, with it being similar to the configuration in China, with plenty of lines and moves on offer.

Respect between two great champions 🤩#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/fbZ6aoKRyw.

“Very difficult to understand. We have been a little bit caught out on Friday with some car behaviour that we did not see all year, but then you can say it is very hot and the tarmac is the different to all the (other) tracks. It looked really good this morning. We seemed to have, at least with Kimi [Antonelli], made a step in understanding. And then, qualifying was a little bit back to what we saw before, just no performance.”.

On Kimi Antonelli’s track limits breach in Q2:.

Recent findings suggest that “Not good, because Q2 you know you are going to get through. You lose a set [of softs] in a qualifying that is so tight, where we are on the back foot. That is not good.”.

Lewis Hamilton says this is the biggest crowd he has ever seen at Sepang, thanking the fans for making it here today. That is actually a bigger compliment than many watching at home may realise. The traffic this weekend has been horrendous. After 10 years without a race in Malaysia, during which time F1 has grown massively, I think they have forgotten how to do traffic management. Shuttles are inconsistent, taxis can’t get in/out, it’s taking forever just to reach the airport a few kilometres away - some fans have been braving the heat and walking. It took over two hours to get back into Kuala Lumpur last night (48km). My understanding is the Bahrainis are organising the race this year, while local forces are handling the traffic outside the circuit.

Industry observers note that “The car has been very good since last week. It is good to come back [from his wrist injury] at such a time and I am enjoying it, fighting for the top three. Even though it was not my finest qualifying session it is a good feeling.

“It is a bit unfortunate we take a penalty on a track where we are that fast but, from eighth, I am confident we can come through the field and come back for a good result.”.

Sources indicate that “I love this energy [from the crowd]. Substantial, big thank you to Malaysia for welcoming us. It is so hot here. I keep saying it, but that has made it a massive challenge for the tyres, the car, the mechanics in the garage. I am really, really thankful to my team. We made so many changes through all these practice sessions. Because the cars are sliding, the tyres are overheating, it was really hard to find a good balance, and we made one last change going into qualifying and I think we hit the sweet spot. To be able to close the gap to two or three tenths to Max [Verstappen], who has been so quick all weekend, is great, and I am so grateful.

“I am much happier with where the car is, but tomorrow is a completely different ballgame. Making these tyres last around this track, they are overheating from the get-go. Every little bit of wheelspin you have, every little snap you have makes a difference of how far you are going to go. I like to think we have got a good balance. Max was really quick on his long runs, so I will just try my best to hold onto him tomorrow.”.

Major disappointment that for Russell. After his win in Baku, where he said he finally felt hooked up to the car, he was desperate to build the momentum. P8, four places behind Antonelli, was not what he would have had in mind. Has it all to do in the race tomorrow.

Excellent (though not unexpected) pole for Verstappen, and a very good P2 for Hamilton. Could be some fireworks on the front row tomorrow.

Antonelli was fourth fastest but has had his lap time deleted for exceeding track limits at turn six. That is a major moment in Q2 and could prove problematic if he gets into Q3. Antonelli appeared to be confused when he was told about his lap deletion over team radio but the on-board view looked pretty clear-cut.

Piastri then comes across the line in third.

Here's the moment Kimi ran wide 👀#F1 #BahrainGP pic.twitter.com/E0VdWdBt8x.

In a recent development, the Dutchman looks in a great spot at the moment to take pole position today and his 1:35.696 is very quick. He is nearly four tenths quicker than Antonelli.

How about the Ferraris? Leclerc was quickest in the middle sector but is nearly three tenths down on Verstappen. Hamilton puts himself into third place. Russell is more than half a second down on Verstappen.

Verstappen has been shown a black and white flag for driving unnecessarily slowly. I doubt he will get a grid penalty for that but it will be a warning for the Dutchman.

Anyway, the drivers, other than Colapinto and Alonso, are on flying laps, with Verstappen presently fastest inthe first sector.

The green light is showing at the end of the pit lane and the second part of qualifying is under way. Like the start of Q1, it is hardly a stampede to go out.

According to recent reports, that has seen the Audi of Hulkenberg drop into the drop zone and the German is out. For contrast, his teammate improves to go into eighth place! Hulkenberg had a massive lock up into turn 14, which proved very costly.

Sources indicate that as it stands, eight of the top nine are remaining in the garage. Russell is in ninth and has not gone out but Gasly above him in eighth has. You would imagine Russell is perfectly safe.

Ocon, in 17th, is quite far off Hulkenberg in 16th and needs more than four tenths to usurp him.

The screens in the media centre here in Sepang tell me that the air temp right now is 32.8C and the track temp is 58C. It feels even hotter. Lots of chat about cooling vests this week, which are optional. George Russell is among the drivers who isn’t using one, which is interesting a) because Russell has suffered badly from heat in the past (Qatar, Singapore) and b) because he claims Mercedes chose to put the development money into car upgrades instead.

It’s an interesting admission. Not everyone is sold on the idea of cooling vests. Ferrari and McLaren will definitely be using them this weekend, for instance. Max Verstappen won’t as he doesn’t like them. Russell thinks the FIA should just develop the tech themselves and it shouldn’t be part of the budget cap.

In a recent development, “Our team have put a lot of emphasis this year on the cockpit temperature,” he remarked. “We won’t be running the cooling vest because we haven’t put the resource into making it robust enough. I feel we need the FIA just to step in and say ‘Here’s some money extra in the cost cap or there’s an external company who’s going to develop it for everybody’. Because we should all be wearing it. When it works, it works great. So, I would like to wear it this week, and I would like to wear it next week. But the team asked me...look, we can develop it, and we can put the money towards it...[but at a cost].

He added: “The top itself is not expensive ..you’ve got to effectively make a system where you can fit a block of dry ice or actual ice, and then has the airflow to circulate the cool water throughout. If that system isn’t robust enough, then suddenly you have no circulation, and then you get hot. You get ambient temperature circulating. The vest is one-design, but the system that circulates the water is different [at different teams].”.

The two Ferraris are on medium tyres but Leclerc still puts himself into second place. He is then displaced by Hamilton, who slots in behind Verstappen. Good times from the Ferraris on the mediums.

What about the McLarens? Norris goes sixth fastest but is more than six tenths down on Verstappen. Then comes Piastri, who goes fourth fastest, just under four tenths off Verstappen.

Arguably the three favourites for pole; Antonelli, Russell and Verstappen, are all on flying laps.

The first sector goes the way of Verstappen, who is purple, and then the Dutchman goes purple in the middle sector.

Antonelli is two tenths faster than his teammate Russell but Verstappen is over half a second quicker than the Mercedes. Hadjar is then second fastest to show the pace in the Red Bull this weekend.

Recent findings suggest that most of the teams waited and waited to come out and then suddenly lots of drivers are sent out, resulting in a queue in the pits! With the high track temperatures and high degradation, the drivers are crawling around on their out laps to preserve these soft tyres.

The top four teams; Mercedes, Red Bull, Ferrari and McLaren, all have a genuine chance of taking pole in Sepang today. I think the true favourites though have to be the Mercedes duo and Max Verstappen but with how close it between all four of the teams you cannot rule anything out.

It is 33 degrees celsius air temperature, with the track temperature up at 58 degrees.

As we know in Malaysia, the weather can change quickly and thunderstorms can roll in quite quickly but it looks like today’s qualifying will be a dry one. This will be one of if not the hottest qualifying sessions of the season, so much so that we are seeing umbrellas going up to get some shade from the sun rather than sheltering from any rain.

This will be crucial to consider after qualifying finishes as there will be some shuffling around:.

There are suggestions that the 30-year-old’s replacement will be Brazilian Ferrari junior Rafael Camara, although nothing has been confirmed on that front. 21-year-old Camara presently leads the Formula 2 championship.

TGR Haas F1 Team and Esteban Ocon will part ways at the conclusion of the 2026 season. With plenty of racing ahead, our focus remains on working together to maximize every opportunity through to the final race of the year.#HaasF1 #F1 pic.twitter.com/4iQAuqnSyA.

Aston Martin have now confirmed their driver line-up for next season, retaining both Fernando Alonso and Lance Stroll. There had been reports that Alonso had been contemplating retirement but the 45-year-old will continue into another season.

Other than the second seat alongside Ollie Bearman at Haas, the only other team to keep an eye on is Racing Bulls, with no definite confirmation on their exact driver line-up for next season.

Ferrari this week have publicly backed their team principal Frederic Vasseur, amid speculation over the Frenchman’s position and comments made by former Red Bull team principal Christian Horner, who said the job at Ferrari would be a “dream job”. Ferrari, who sit second in the constructors’ standings, have not won the drivers’ championship since 2007 (Kimi Raikkonen) and the constructors’ since 2008. Here is a snippet from Tom Cary’s piece on the matter:.

In a hastily convened media call on Tuesday morning, Maria Conti, Ferrari’s chief communication officer, said the Scuderia had decided to glitch a vote of confidence in Vasseur in response “not just to the story of Mr Horner, but in general, the speculation about Fred”.

Industry observers note that “Ferrari has made its choices,” Conti said. “We have confidence – full confidence – in Fred Vasseur and in his team, and we continue to do so.

“At this time, it’s really notable that the team remains united and cohesive, and we are focused with all the energy on the work ahead.”.

In a recent development, “It is great to be back [in Malaysia]. I am really enjoying the track. We have had some wonderful races here over time. It is actually the 20th time we have been here, it started in 1999, and it is really exciting to be back. I really enjoyed getting out on the track and watching the cars closely.

Recent findings suggest that “The drivers are super fit and they have some cooling but it is not easy. But you almost cannot get enough fluid through your body before your stomach gives up. Having this race and Singapore back-to-back increases that challenge.”.

Especially with the massive upgrade they have brought this weekend, Mercedes’ lead at the summit is looking unassailable right now.

Recent findings suggest that almost nine years ago to the day, Max Verstappen took just his second race victory in Formula 1. Lewis Hamilton, who took pole position, and Daniel Ricciardo joined Verstappen on the podium. Despite being nine years ago, plenty of drivers still on the grid were racing that weekend. Here they are and who they were racing for:.

Max Verstappen (Red Bull) Lewis Hamilton (Mercedes) Valtteri Bottas (Mercedes) Esteban Ocon (Force India)Nico Hulkenberg (Renault)Sergio Perez (Force India)Fernando Alonso (McLaren)Lance Stroll (Williams)Carlos Sainz (Toro Rosso)Pierre Gasly (Toro Rosso).

In a recent development, with Russell winning in Baku and Antonelli finishing fifth, the latter’s championship lead was cut to 66 points. If Russell is going to usurp his teammate, he is going to need a few more similar results to last weekend due to the size of Antonelli’s lead. If Antonelli were to suffer a retirement, then that completely changes the outlook.

According to recent reports, formula One returns to Malaysia for round 16 of the season for the Bahrain Grand Prix. That probably sounds strange but after the Bahrain Grand Prix was originally postponed in March, F1 reinstated it to the calendar with Malaysia hosting it because of the ongoing war in the Middle East. Despite being held in Malaysia, Bahrain have retained the naming rights for the event, which is officially known as the Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia. The last time Formula One was in Malaysia was nine years ago back in 2017, when a young whippersnapper named Max Verstappen, still four years away from winning his first world championship, claimed just his second victory.

According to recent reports, last time out around the streets of Baku, Mercedes’ George Russell claimed victory at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix, pipping Verstappen by just a tenth of a second. That was Russell’s first grand prix win since June and cuts his team-mate Kimi Antonelli’s lead in the drivers’ standings to 66 points. Antonelli had a challenging weekend in Baku, starting 16th after a crash in qualifying and coming home in fifth to see his championship lead to Russell cut by 15 points.

Industry observers note that verstappen was quickest in first practice yesterday, with the Ferrari of Charles Leclerc fastest in second practice. Mercedes, 160 points clear at the top of the constructors’ standings, have brought significant upgrades this weekend, which includes a newly introduced floor, rear suspension and rear corner. It is the team’s first significant car patch since the Canadian Grand at the end of May.

In a recent development, this race in Malaysia represents the second leg of the season’s first flyaway triple header, with the Singapore Grand Prix to come next weekend, so the demands on the teams and the drivers are incredibly high. Qualifying from Sepang gets under way at 9am (GMT).

  • Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Sandro Tonali is missing from Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town due to illness.
  • The Italy international was a surprise absentee from the Lilywhites' squad against the Tractor Boys, as Conor Gallagher was instead given the nod in central midfield with Mateus Fernandes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 14:40, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 14:53.

Tottenham Hotspur manager Roberto De Zerbi has confirmed that Sandro Tonali is missing from Saturday's Premier League clash with Ipswich Town due to illness.

The Italy international was a surprise absentee from the Lilywhites' squad against the Tractor Boys, as Conor Gallagher was instead given the nod in central midfield with Mateus Fernandes.

Tonali was not name-checked in De Zerbi's pre-game press conference, and the expectation was that the former Newcastle United man would make his 11th Premier League start of the season.

However, Tonali's perfect starting streak in the top-flight campaign is now over, and De Zerbi explained the midfielder's absence when speaking to reporters ahead of kickoff.

"(The reasons for the changes are) a combination of physical condition (and defeat to Leeds). Many players, they came back (from international duty) not in the right condition. (Sandro) Tonali was sick for a couple of days. Rodrigo Bentancur arrived yesterday, just yesterday working with us," De Zerbi mentioned.

Recent findings suggest that "I am lucky because I have a great squad. Many players. All players are very close in level so now we start a very tough period of three games in a row. We are ready.".

De Zerbi made a total of six changes to his starting lineup from the XI that began the 1-0 loss to Ipswich Town before the international break, including a landmark start in attack for Luca Williams-Barnett.

The 18-year-old makes his full Premier League debut at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium as part of a much-changed attack, which also sees Dominic Solanke and James Maddison replace Omar Marmoush and Archie Gray.

Further back, Destiny Udogie and Marcos Senesi have displaced Andy Robertson and Micky van de Ven, who are on the bench alongside Marmoush, Gray and the returning Savio and Lucas Bergvall.

Tonali has played over 500 more Premier League minutes than Gallagher so far this season, but the England international nevertheless leads his Italian colleague in several per 90 metrics.

As per the comparison chart, Gallagher ranks higher in terms of duels won, tackles and interceptions per 90, as well as winning more free kicks and committing more fouls.

The former Chelsea man also attempts more shots per game and boasts a higher ratio of shots on target, but Tonali triumphs in terms of successful passes, big chances created and dribble success rate.

However, with a fully-fit Maddison back in the starting lineup, Spurs should have little in the way of creativity concerns as De Zerbi's men bid to return to winning ways on home territory.

#37433. Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

Can we regrow damaged seagrass meadows?

📅 28 Oct 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (800 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany.
  • Recent findings suggest that they only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow.
  • In a recent development, the scientists see the work as critical.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Half a dozen divers are navigating the cold waters of the Baltic Sea off the coast of Dahme, a small beach town in northern Germany. Keeping the roots intact, conservationists carefully lift shoots from a donor meadow of seagrass and place them in a bag.

Recent findings suggest that they only take a few shoots from each spot, which will be planted where the conservationists hope to regrow another meadow. They've already picked out a prime area for the young plants, which need sandy sediment, shelter from waves and currents and sufficient light and oxygen to thrive.

In a recent development, the scientists see the work as critical. Myriam Spicka, who heads the NGO Seagrass Conservation, notes she has "seen the changes" in the more than 30 years she's been diving. And she is not the only one who has witnessed the destruction.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Scientists estimate that around 60% of the Baltic coast's seagrass meadows have disappeared.

"That's the bad news," said marine ecologist Thorsten Reusch from the GEOMAR Helmholtz Center for Ocean Research Kiel . "The good news is that the decline has stopped.".

Sources indicate that underwater seagrass meadows feed and shelter fish, crabs, shellfish and many other species. They improve water quality and slow waves, helping protect shores from erosion. And they store carbon in the seabed about 30 to 50 times faster than forests.

Industry observers note that around 70 species of seagrass can be found along the coasts of more than 150 countries. Some grow just below the surface, others at depths of 60 meters or almost 200 feet.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Recent findings suggest that "Some countries have far more seagrass, particularly in the Indo-Pacific," stated Reusch. "There, it can play a major role in their carbon balance.".

Sources indicate that but the value of seagrass goes beyond carbon storage. Its meadows in the Baltic are among the sea's most valuable habitats. They shelter wildlife, stabilize the seabed and act as natural filters by trapping particles and nutrients.

Planting individual seagrass shoots is painstaking work so people like Reinhard Helbig are trying to make it easier.

According to recent reports, through ZosteraTec, the start-up he co-founded, he helps restore marine habitats, including seagrass meadows damaged by offshore activity, such as wind farm construction. His work begins on the beach.

"Stormy weather helps us. Waves and currents wash seagrass out of the seabed. A day or two later, it washes up here, still fresh," he remarked.

It has been revealed that the collected shoots are grown and multiplied in ZosteraTec's aquaculture. Several months later, the marine saplings are laid on a plant support. A specially developed machine binds the planted strands with biodegradable thread. The resulting lengths can be laid on the seabed with less diving work.

Recent findings suggest that "We plant here on land to cut down on underwater work. That means fewer dives, and we can do the painstaking work on shore," Helbig noted.

Researchers at the Geomar Helmholtz Center in Kiel are also testing latest ways to restore seagrass across larger areas, including using seeds.

Marine ecologist Esther Thomsen reaches into an aquarium tank and pulls out a flowerpot containing seagrass.

Industry observers note that "Ten percent of the plants in our meadows produce seeds. You can clearly see the seeds sitting inside the seed pod," she said.

"The big advantage of restoring meadows from seed is greater genetic diversity. And in the future, we should be able to sow seeds over much larger areas," explained Thomsen.

Reusch from Geomar said they at the moment "think the most promising way to grow meadows that can withstand climate change is to plant individual shoots as a foundation, then sow seeds between them to increase genetic diversity.".

Whether a planting mission is successful is revealed months or even years later.

It has been revealed that thomsen and her colleagues are visiting the first seagrass meadow planted in Germany's Baltic waters in 2021. The divers count shoots, check how densely they grow and record how the meadow has developed.

They then compare it with the donor meadow that supplied the plants. Only that comparison reveals whether the newly introduced crop has merely survived or is beginning to function more like a natural one.

Industry observers note that "We've just checked the seagrass meadow, and it's really dense. We counted lots of shoots per square," Thomsen said. "It's looking really good.".

💡 Key Takeaways

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Ruben Amorim will be up against Massimiliano Alvini tomorrow evening, and as the stats show, they are two very different managers.

Recent findings suggest that as highlighted by Gazzetta dello Sport, there is one interesting stat to highlight to introduce the game. In terms of shots per game, it will be the second-ranked team and against the 17th-ranked team. That in itself won’t raise any eyebrows, but the fact that Milan are the ones in 17th place will.

In a recent development, read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Recent findings suggest that the Rossoneri have mustered a mere 126 shots so far, while Frosinone are quite far ahead at 221. On the flip side, the newly-promoted side have only scored one more goal than Milan (24 vs. 23), which is what makes this game so interesting.

Amorim has made it clear from the start that he wants to dominate each game. That shows in the possession, as Milan are third in Serie A with an average of 59% so far, and they also rank high in terms of passes per game.

The shots are where they fall short, even if they average over two goals per game. There are several reasons for this, but most of it can be attributed to Amorim’s recent arrival and the fact that he has experimented rather extensively.

During today’s presser, he even said that they haven’t done anywhere near enough to enter the penalty box more often, which tends to mean more shots.

Industry observers note that in the build-up, for example, the Rossoneri move the ball forward at an average speed of 1.30 meters per second, which is the slowest in Serie A. Alvini’s Frosinone, on the other hand, are great at vertical football: the ball moves toward the opponent’s penalty box at 2.51 meters per second, the best rate in the league.

The Ciociari are masters of rapid counterattacks, so much so that on only 40 occasions have they built plays with ten or more passes. Milan, meanwhile, have 203.

In a recent development, everything starts in the defence phase for Frosinone. Indeed, they always attempt to win the ball back inside the opponent’s half, which is proven by the index that measures the intensity of pressing in the attacking zone (they are first in Serie A).

Sources indicate that milan? They are eighth, despite being – along with Como – the team to have scored the most goals (4) from a ball recovered while pressing.

The difference between the two is well explained by the so-called “pressed sequences”, that is, the number of actions in open play in which a team manages to interrupt the opponent’s build-up within three passes or less, before the ball goes beyond the halfway line.

Industry observers note that on that front, Frosinone are also first (161), while Milan are only 15th (102). Having said all of this, as the pink newspaper concludes, we should expect a spectacular match tomorrow. Both teams will stick to their respective game, which bodes well.

Premier League identify SIX key refereeing errors in one weekend as boss Howard Webb prepares to appear in front of clubs after Arsenal blunder

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 06:08 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 19 November 2026.
  • The Premier League have ruled that referees made a staggering six incorrect decisions in the latest round of matches as officials endured their worst weekend of the season so far.
  • It was unanimously ruled that referee Farai Hallam should have awarded Kai Havertz a penalty after he was tugged in the area during Arsenal's victory over Hull City, despite being in an offside position.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 06:08 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 03:22 EST, 19 November 2026.

The Premier League have ruled that referees made a staggering six incorrect decisions in the latest round of matches as officials endured their worst weekend of the season so far.

It was unanimously ruled that referee Farai Hallam should have awarded Kai Havertz a penalty after he was tugged in the area during Arsenal's victory over Hull City, despite being in an offside position.

That is because the laws state that if a foul occurs before an offside offence, a penalty should be awarded.

Although Havertz was in an offside position, he had not committed an offence as he neither played the ball nor interfered with play.

The key match incidents panel (KMI) stated: 'Given the chronology of events, a penalty should have been awarded.'.

Farai Hallam's decision not to award Kai Havertz a penalty was deemed incorrect by the key match incidents panel.

Coventry were wrongly denied a spot-kick in their defeat to Everton after James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair.

Sources indicate that 1. Everton vs Coventry City: Frank Lampard's side should have been awarded a penalty when James Tarkowski pulled Caleb Yirenkyi's hair.

Recent findings suggest that 2. Everton vs Coventry City: The Toffees' second goal, scored by Thierno Barry should not have stood as the ball was adjudged to have gone into the back of the net off his hand.

3. Arsenal vs Hull City: Kai Havertz was denied a penalty after being dragged down. The referee did not award a spot-kick because Havertz in an offside position. However, that decision was incorrect, as he was not committing an offside offence and a spot-kick should therefore have been awarded.

It has been revealed that 4. Crystal Palace vs Liverpool: Palace were awarded a penalty in the last minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool after Milos Kerkez and Dario Osario clashed heads in the penalty area. The panel saw this as a natural coming together.

5. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: A penalty was given after Abdoul Ouattara tumbled over. The referee gave a foul against Lewis Cook despite Ouattara stepping across him.

Sources indicate that 6. Ipswich Town vs Bournemouth: Marcus Tavernier should have seen a second yellow card for time-wasting.

They did, however, praise the VAR for asking the referee to review the incident on the monitor, even though Hallam stuck with his on-field call after watching it back.

In the same weekend, Tottenham Hotspur complained to Pro Ref after Jayden Bogle's heavy challenge on Mathys Tel's ankle, which forced him off injured.

Spurs felt Bogle should have seen red, particularly after Crystal Palace's Jean-Philippe Mateta was sent off for a similar incident the week prior.

Reviewing the decision, the KMI panel were split but eventually concluded that the foul lacked 'the speed, force or intensity' to be considered serious foul play.

Two of the five panellists, however, felt that the challenge merited a red card.

Meanwhile, Crystal Palace's consolation penalty in the 92nd minute of their 3-1 defeat to Liverpool should never have been awarded.

The KMI panel unanimously agreed the referee was wrong to award a penalty when Milos Kerkez and Dario Osorio clashed heads while contesting the ball, with contact inevitable given both players were jumping.

However, VAR's decision not to intervene was supported because it was not a 'clear and obvious error'.

It is the second penalty incident in as many weeks that went against Liverpool after Alexander Isak was wrongfully denied a spot-kick against Arsenal.

On the opposite side of Merseyside, James Tarkowski was fortunate not to concede a penalty for pulling Caleb Yirenkyi's hair during Everton's win over Coventry City, with the score still 0-0 at the time. The panel found that Coventry should have been awarded a penalty while Tarkowski should have been booked.

Industry observers note that last season, that incident would likely have resulted in a straight red card. However, the guidance changed this term with red cards only brandished for excessive force.

Thierno Barry's goal that gave Everton the lead faced scrutiny as three panellists believed it should have been disallowed on the pitch, with the 'balance of probability suggesting the ball accidentally struck Barry's hand before directly entering the goal'.

There were also two incorrect decisions in Bournemouth's victory over Ipswich Town.

Recent findings suggest that bournemouth defender Marcus Tavernier should have been sent off for a second yellow card in the 96th minute for delaying the restart during their 2-1 win, the panel found. However, it was a close call as the panel voted 3-2 against the decision.

Ipswich's scored penalty was also deemed wrongly awarded, with Abdoul Ouattara stepping across Lewis Cook to win the spot-kick rather than being fouled by the defender.

The KMI panel consists of a representative from the Premier League and Pro Ref alongside three former managers or players and meets after every round of Premier League matches to evaluate significant refereeing decisions.

Ref boss Howard Webb will speak to Premier League clubs at a routine meeting on Thursday.

While the panel is not latest, this is the first season their findings have been publicly released in Pro Ref's drive for greater transparency and accountability.

Pro Ref boss Howard Webb is due to appear in front of clubs on Thursday at a routine Premier League meeting.

And in more positive news for Webb, he will be able to share that VAR delays are down this season after increasing the bar for interventions.

Meanwhile, the KMI panel have assessed 296 decisions this season - only six of which have been judged to be wrong post-VAR.

  • Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly prepared to make a 'significant' effort to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela.
