📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Sully | 21 Nov 2026 14:53, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 15:57.

Tottenham Hotspur are reportedly prepared to make a 'significant' effort to sign Monza striker Gustavo Varela.

The 21-year-old completed a permanent move to Monza from Benfica in the summer after spending last season on loan at Gil Vicente.

The Portuguese forward netted seven times in 33 games during that loan spell, including six Primeira Liga goals to help Gil Vicente achieve a six-place finish.

Varela has already passed that tally during his short time in Italy, having scored 11 goals in as many competitive matches for Monza.

In fact, he presently leads Serie A's scoring charts with nine goals, including five goals in the club's last five league games before the international window.

Having stood out in a struggling Monza side, Varela is already attracting plenty of transfer interest despite being under contract until 2030 with the club he joined in the summer.

Liverpool are among those who have already been linked with a potential swoop for the in-form striker.

Tottenham Hotspur are also in the mix, with Il Giorno reporting the North London club are willing to pay a 'significant' fee to win the race for Varela's signature.

There is a belief that an offer of €35m (£29.4m) could be enough to persuade Monza to part ways in the winter market.

Like Spurs, Brighton & Hove Albion are prepared to splash the cash to sign Varela, who is also attracting interest from Juventus and Napoli, the latter of whom could offer Giovanni Simeone in a potential deal.

Meanwhile, Benfica have the opportunity to match any offer for Varela, which was a clause included as part of the agreement that saw him join Monza.

Roberto De Zerbi decided against naming Richarlison in his Premier League squad despite the fact the Brazilian failed to secure a move away in the summer.

Having been deemed surplus to requirements, the Everton forward is widely expected to leave when the transfer window opens in the latest year.

Spurs are therefore looking to bolster their number nine options and recruit someone who can challenge Dominic Solanke and summer signing Omar Marmoush for a starting spot.

The club's need for a striker is also influenced by the fact Solanke and Marmoush have netted just a goal apiece in the Premier League.

If this is Tuchel-ball, if this is the way Thomas Tuchel wants England to play, then yes, please. More of the same; bring it on. The standard is set.

Recent findings suggest that england’s DNA? This was a total-football annihilation of a top nation. Croatia, 14th in the world and fierce competitors, were cowed and humiliated at home in this Nations League tie. This was the biggest defeat in their proud history – seventh heaven for England, and hell for the hosts.

In a recent development, the visitors were sublime. Harry Kane (twice – 89 goals now for his country), Jude Bellingham and Anthony Gordon all scored and were outstanding. Bukayo Saka also struck twice. Alex Scott made his first start and will take some dislodging. The Bournemouth midfielder was slick with a snap – perpetual, intelligent, smooth motion.

Harry Kane at the DOUBLE! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿The Three Lions have FIVE in Rijeka 🦁 pic.twitter.com/BRnVXADtHC.

Luka Modric has had the most extraordinary career but he was emphatically second best here and was subbed off on 57 minutes at 5-0. He looked bereft, having had Scott and Elliot Anderson run all over him and Mateo Kovacic.

We came out of the World Cup wondering if Tuchel really had an idea of how he can get England over the line. After last Saturday’s defeat by world and European champions Spain, followed by Tuesday’s win over the Czech Republic we still did not know.

But here the standard was set – it was an exhilarating example of the football England are capable of. On display we saw the speed, the movement, the passes under pressure, the ambition, the control and aggression. This was the full package. Bottle it. Bag it. Believe it.

Sources indicate that croatia have an ageing team and are in transition, but they were left looking callow. It looked as though it was men against boys. There were plenty of boys in the stands, with 6,200 children allowed in for what was supposed to be a behind-closed-doors fixture – Croatia’s punishment for crowd trouble.

In a recent development, their upcoming head coach Slaven Bilic would doubtless have been relieved that the match was not played in front of the usual, passionate, partisan crowd. Even then some of the kids booed and left early. Bilic looked shell-shocked. As well he might.

And Saka makes it FOUR! ⚽️⚽️⚽️⚽️England break to devastating effect - Croatia are reeling... pic.twitter.com/60EgNt4cfh.

It has been revealed that it was 4-0 at half-time. It could easily have been 7-1 – Kovacic missed a sitter for Croatia at 3-0 and Gordon should have had a hat-trick. How significant is it that England’s three most dangerous players do not play in the Premier League? Probably not very. But the fact they turn out for Real Madrid, Barcelona and Bayern Munich is. They performed like the top players their clubs think they clearly are.

According to recent reports, gordon heads in to make it THREE! 💥England are cruising 🛳️ pic.twitter.com/nqwUxFmkof.

According to recent reports, kane’s commitment was incredible. At one stage Croatia substitute Kristijan Jakić threatened to break clear but was stopped by England’s last man tracking back. It was Kane, one cap short of equalling Peter Shilton’s all-time record of 125 appearances, and it was already 5-0 when that happened.

Industry observers note that these could be exciting times for England. Times when they have shaken off the debate over how well or otherwise they did at the World Cup and moved on. Tuchel has talked up that third-place finish; we have tended to dwell on the semi-final exit to Argentina.

And now? If Tuchel does go and win a trophy for England, he will be talking about this game. Previously he referenced the 5-0 demolition of Serbia in Belgrade, during the World Cup qualification. But the Serbians were a rabble. Croatia are not, but were made to look so on Saturday.

Where will this sit among England performances? There was the 2-1 victory away to Italy at the beginning of the Euro 2024 qualification campaign in March 2023. Before that, the 3-2 win away to Spain in 2018, also in the Nations League. But England were more thrilling here. Do we have to go back to 5-1 in Munich in 2001?

The concern will be the familiar England problem of looking like world-beaters in the autumn and worn out by the time a tournament comes around in the summer. But against Croatia there was control and authority as they raised their chances of finishing in the top two and qualifying for next March’s quarter-finals.

Recent findings suggest that the goals rained in – even if the best remained the first as Marc Guéhi intercepted a clearance, Scott took the ball on the half-turn and found Bellingham. He slid it through to Kane who finished high into the net. What a goal.

It has been revealed that bellingham ➡️ Kane! ⚽️The Three Lions lead in Rijeka with their first shot on target 🎯 pic.twitter.com/ZLcnGLvj3z.

What a touch from Anthony Gordon! 🔥The Barca man squares it to the Real Madrid man and England lead 2-0 ⚽️⚽️ pic.twitter.com/31Y1Ojx44M.

Even before half-time England were not finished as Bellingham crossed low from the left and found Saka, who found the back of the net.

Sources indicate that after the break, the hunger remained insatiable. Anderson was sent down the right and Kane slid in. Croatia then lost the ball sloppily inside their own area, Kane thought about shooting but unselfishly fed Saka, who claimed a second goal.

In a recent development, saka should have had a hat-trick before substitute Morgan Rogers wrapped up the scoring, collecting a ball over the top from the relentless Bellingham – once again captain after Kane went off – and finishing with ease after rounding the goalkeeper. It was a third assist for Bellingham and a seventh goal for England. It could have been double figures.

According to recent reports, SEVENTH heaven for England! 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿Morgan Rogers is the latest player to put his name on the scoresheet... ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/H5txZRVgLC.

Absolutely [that was the 90-minute performance we’ve been looking for]. And from the first until the last minute from everyone who started and everyone who came on. Congratulations to the team.

Very, very impressive [to do this] on an away pitch. We created so many chances in the first 40 minutes. We were so fluid from the start. I looked at the clock and thought ‘Oh, this has been a good three minutes, this has been a good seven minutes…’ and it never stopped.

We kept the pace up and played through the gaps, stayed hungry in our counter-pressing and defending.

We played humble and always got the basics right.

According to recent reports, unbelievable from start to finish. We spoke a lot about having a 90-minute game in which we were dominant with and without the ball and that was it out there. We’re at our best when we’re brave and we’re physically overpowering. When we make it a Premier League game and they couldn’t live with our pace, our movement, our runs. And we were clinical.

Industry observers note that there’s freedom. All four of us [him, Bellingham, Saka and Gordon] can play in the 10 pocket, play as the nine. I can play as a midfielder. We’re good enough and smart enough so if we lose the ball we can cover in midfield and defence. That’s the way we want to play. It’s so hard for them to pick a man and press. Every man was at the highest level.

Industry observers note that beautiful hotel, lovely weather, we could easily have fallen into that holiday mode. It’s an unusual situation for us. We’ve never been away this long in this kind of camp and that’s the perfect end to the week,.

[And now to equal Peter Shilton’s record 125th cap on Tuesday?] That would be nice. That’s why he keeps taking me off, to rest me for the next game. That’s what he said to me after. I’ll be ready to start on Tuesday.

In a recent development, an amazing night for us. We came out from the start on top and played with high energy and we punished them.

It was special and fun to play. We were really clinical today. Two goals for England is always a nice feeling.

We demonstrated the hunger, passion and quality we had. A mixture of everything we wanted to show.

According to recent reports, [Bellingham] was amazing tonight. He deserved man of the match and deserves to be player of the year.

At least the Croatia fans did not seem too dispirited, the kids smiling and waving at the camera, despite the utter trouncing their team took.

England were terrific but how much of that was because Croatia were terrible will be open to debate.

Pickford will start for England in the Nations League tie against Croatia, and next Tuesday’s fixture at home to the Czech Republic, having missed out on the past two games.

Trafford was in goal for the 3-2 loss to Spain and the 2-0 victory away to the Czechs and although Thomas Tuchel has remarked Pickford remains his first choice it is known that he and his coaching staff are huge admirers of Leeds United’s new goalkeeper.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is expected to drop back down to the substitutes’ bench for England’s third Nations League game against Croatia in Rijeka.

According to recent reports, jude Bellingham is also in line for a recall, most likely in place of Morgan Rogers, while Tuchel had been hopeful of Ezri Konsa returning to fitness to replace Trevoh Chalobah in the centre of defence. Goalkeeper Jordan Pickford replaces James Trafford.

In a recent development, uefa fined the Croatian football federation £80,000 and ordered them to play their next Uefa-sanctioned home match behind closed doors because of their fans’ racist chanting and for fireworks offences during a Nations League match against France in 2025. Croatia have played Fifa-sanctioned World Cup qualifiers and friendlies at home in front of fans since but tonight is the first in Uefa competition and hence the ban.

Industry observers note that however, a caveat in Uefa’s disciplinary regulations allows the home federation in such circumstances to fill the ground to 75 per cent of its capacity with “children up to the age of 14 (duly accompanied) from schools and/or football academies invited to the match free of charge”. And given the scrum outside the stadium this afternoon, that is what is happening.

Good afternoon and welcome to live coverage of England’s Uefa Nations League Group A3 match against Croatia in Rijeka. Matches between the two are relatively frequent – 12 in 30 years. Croatia have beaten England three times in the 10 competitive meetings, home and away in qualification for Euro 2008, which dealt the England manager a blow from which he could not recover, and the World Cup semi-final in Moscow in 2018.

The extraordinary thing about both the first two defeats – the ‘Wally with the Brolly’ match in November 2007, Steve McLaren’s last in charge, and the home tie on October 10 2006 – is that Luka Modric played in both. And now eight days shy of 20 years since his first appearance against England, he is still running their midfield at the age of 41.

England have had the upper hand since Russia, winning in the Nations League at Wembley in 2018, opening their Euro 2020 campaign with a 1-0 victory by virtue of Raheem Sterling’s goal and then in June when they were at their fluent best, a rare occurrence, in the second half of their first World Cup group game to push on from 2-2 to finish 4-2.

In a recent development, slaven Bilic, manager from 2006-12, is back in charge for his second spell but his squad still relies heavily on experienced players. Modric is the eldest but is joined by greybeard stalwarts Ivan Perisic, Ante Budimir and Andrej Kramaric, both 35. Spain hammered them 4-1 in midweek after they had started with a 2-1 victory over Czech Republic in Prague.

England, who rattled Spain and should have gone 3-1 up but lost 3-2, were much better in the second half in Prague against a team reduced to 10 men and deserved their 2-0 win, have played at the tiny Stadion Rujevica (capacity 8,279) once before, drawing 0-0 in 2018.

Thomas Tuchel, who changed three of his back four on Tuesday, may stick with Lewis Hall after he made a positive impression in combination with Anthony Gordon. As for Trent Alexander-Arnold, who set up the first goal, Tuchel does not go out of his way to undermine the perception that for all his unique quality, he just doesn’t fancy the Real Madrid right-back at all.

It’s up to Alexander-Arnold to make a compelling case if picked today or at Wembley on Tuesday to persuade the German head coach not to restore his beloved if brittle ‘Reecey’ James at the first opportunity.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The Volkswagen Group on Thursday posted its worst quarterly numbers in more than a decade.

Sources indicate that the company reported an operating loss of €5.86 billion (roughly $6.53 billion) during July, August and September. One-off costs, not least a massive writedown in its stake in struggling sister company Porsche, explained the vast bulk of the losses.

The world's second-largest carmaker is battling mounting competition from and falling demand in the core Chinese market.

It is pursuing a major restructuring and downsizing program, trying to bolster falling profit margins, and executives stated the difficulties highlighted the urgency of this process.

Recent findings suggest that "The nine-month results make one thing clear: We cannot afford to lose any time. We must act swiftly and decisively," chief financial officer Arno Antlitz remarked in a video statement.

The results were the latest reminder of the pressure on VW — and the wider German and Western automotive industry — to react to increasing competition in China, high costs and practical difficulties moving towards electric car production, and unpredictable and rising tariff burdens, thanks in no small part to US President Donald Trump.

Here are some of the key Q3 figures:.

And here are some of the key year-to-date 9-month figures:.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

VW shares were already at their lowest levels in well over 10 years prior to Thursday's announcements, after months of difficult headlines and the ongoing prepares to shed tens of thousands of jobs and reduce production capacities.

Perhaps as a result of this, the stock dipped briefly as markets opened and the news was published, but then started to rally as the day progressed.

By midday in Frankfurt, VW shares had climbed by 2% compared to their prices at the start of trading on the DAX.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

CEO Oliver Blume prepares to shed around 100,000 jobs across the group, which includes the Audi and Porsche brands, in the coming years though a combination of layoffs and not replacing departing or retiring personnel.

Sources indicate that multiple factors are contributing to this. They include increased competition from Chinese manufacturers, falling revenues in China, changeable US auto tariffs under President Donald Trump, different staffing requirements when manufacturing electric cars and difficulties moving towards making and selling more electric cars at the pace once designated by political leaders.

Up to four plants in Germany could face closure as part of the strategy, which has met with considerable union resistance and could lead to strikes starting next year.

CFO Antlitz said the figures highlighted the urgency underlying these intends, saying the tech giant needed to increase its profit margins by 2030 to solidify its finances.

Antlitz remarked the operating return on sales was only 3.8% in the first nine months of the year, even before the one-off writedowns hitting the bottom line.

"That is not enough in the long term," he said.

As part of its restructuring program, the VW Group aims to restore an operating profit margin of between 8-10% by 2030.

This year, amid one-off costs now totaling in the region of €10 billion, it expects a profit margin of no more than 1%, compared to prior forecasts in the region of 5%.

Mauricio Pochettino has issued a rallying cry to Manchester United supporters, promising that this is going to be a 'special season' despite their dismal start which sees them 18th in the Premier League with just one win from their opening 10 games.

The latest Red Devils head coach landed in Manchester on Wednesday morning, hopping straight off a private jet to meet his new players, hours after leading the USA in his final game as their boss.

And during a busy first day among his new surroundings, the Argentine sent a direct message to the club's fanbase as he preached for unity.

'Hi Reds, here's it's Mauricio Pochettino,' he mentioned via a video posted on United's X account at 7.15pm on Wednesday evening.

'I am looking forward to meeting you guys. I hear so many good things about you.

'I hope we bring all the happiness working together and connecting together.

A message from Mauricio 💬❤️🤳 #ShotOnSnapdragon pic.twitter.com/2lBLkMaGY6.

Mauricio Pochettino addressed Manchester United fans directly on Wednesday evening after starting work officially as their new head coach.

The new Red Devils head coach has promised a 'special season' in a direct message to fans.

Pochettino poses at his unveiling with United director of football Jason Wilcox on Wednesday.

'This is going to be a special season to support and to make our players to fight on the field and to get the results that we deserve.'.

In a second message in his native Spanish, Pochettino expanded further: 'This message is about being united, like the name Manchester United. We all need to work together.

'I hope to bring the happy moments that this club deserves and create the unity that every team needs so that the players can be at their best on the pitch.'.

Those messages came less than eight hours after arriving in England. He landed in Manchester at 11.32am on Wednesday and immediately headed to their Carrington training base where he took a tour and met players and staff.

According to recent reports, speaking to the club's media channels earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino stated: 'Thank you so much, I'm very excited to be here. It's an honour, it's a privilege to be in this amazing club. I'm looking forward to starting work.'.

The club then officially welcomed the upcoming manager on their website, writing: 'Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

According to recent reports, 'Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham Hotspur, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.'.

Pochettino had made a promise to end Man City's dominance as United manager in his last interview as United States national team coach on Tuesday evening.

He took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet chartered by the club after his final match on American soil, which saw the US beat Haiti 2-0 in Cincinnati.

But before becoming airborne, Pochettino had time for a final statement Stateside, after being taunted that 'Manchester is blue, and will always be blue' by one of his interviewers.

Earlier on Wednesday, Pochettino made his way to Carrington straight after landing in Manchester, meeting players and staff and taking a tour.

The Argentine took off from northern Kentucky in a private jet last night and landed at 11.32am.

The manager shared a picture from his journey as he prepared to touch down at the airport (Source: Instagram/Mauricio Pochettino).

According to recent reports, 'No way,' he shook his head. 'You will see.'.

According to recent reports, 'Give me time. Give me time and then that - that's going to change.'.

Pochettino also shared a poignant farewell message to his US set-up, days after breaking down in tears in a press conference ahead of his penultimate time in charge.

Man United fans may also have been pleased to read of Pochettino's new-found love of John Denver's song Country Roads in his goodbye message, a song which is played before kick-off at Old Trafford.

'It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together.' Pochettino captioned a carousel of photos of his time in the role. 'I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

'From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.

It has been revealed that 'When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something key for the future of soccer in this country.

The plane believed to be carrying Pochettino and his staff was hired by Manchester United.

'This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made new friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

Industry observers note that 'Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at (the US national team) and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

Recent findings suggest that 'Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

'I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.'.

Pochettino had previously explained his emotions as stemming from how difficult the decision had been to leave the national team and re-start at Old Trafford.

Industry observers note that ‘I haven't prepared a speech, I'm talking with my heart,’ he said on Friday. ‘It's difficult for me to talk now because I am a very emotional guy.

‘When these moments arrive, it is always tough. Normally it is the opposite – you have been sacked! You cry because you want to stay.

‘I think it was one of the most difficult decisions of our career, but you have to move forward.

It has been revealed that ‘Not too many opportunities can happen in your career with a side like Manchester United. That is difficult to turn down when it arrives.

‘In some part it’s a very sad decision, in another part we are professional and we are trying to make our dreams come true. We are excited for that step forward.'.

Man United first made contact with Pochettino following their breathless 4-4 draw against Aston Villa in their last match before the international break.

The Man United hierarchy had previously given former head coach Michael Carrick a stay of execution amid a worrying start to the season, but as they prepared to head into the two-week pause in the relegation zone, the board became keen to make a change.

An agonising wait for Carrick followed, with the club legend taking training for multiple sessions at the start of the week as his future was openly mulled by executives including CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

After the duo returned from Monaco, where they had flown to speak to co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe about Carrick's future, the 45-year-old was finally dispatched last Thursday morning.

In their statement regarding Pochettino's arrival on Wednesday, United also confirmed the exits of Carrick and Co, writing: 'The club can confirm the departures of Travis Binnion, Jonny Evans, Steve Holland, Craig Mawson and Jonathan Woodgate alongside Michael Carrick.

'We would like to thank the group for their total commitment, dedication and professionalism, and we wish them all good luck for the future.'.

Pochettino's United States farewell match went off in pitch-perfect style, which allowed thoughts to swiftly move to the next task at hand after the final whistle.

Christian Pulisic helped make sure that Pochettino's reign in charge ended on a high note.

The manager will now focus his attentions on getting Man United out of the relegation zone.

'When you finish the game, you start in your mind to think about different things,' Pochettino remarked after the win. 'Of course, it's tough because it's emotional. Because I really love these guys, and I love the players. I love the staff. I love the fans and everything.'.

Travelling with Pochettino were outgoing USMNT first-team coach Miguel D'Agostino, strength and conditioning coach Silvia Tuya and analyst Alec Scott, while his assistant Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez as well as Pochettino's son and fitness coach Sebastiano have already begun preparing for Sunday's matchup with Liverpool at Anfield.

Man United paid a staggering £10million to cleave Pochettino and his staff away from the United States, after the head coach signed a new contract with the national team in the wake of this summer's World Cup.

Recent findings suggest that the quick turnaround means Pochettino will be able to work with the players as they begin reporting back from international duty. Furthermore, he is expected to speak to club media before conducting his pre-match press conference around lunchtime on Friday.

Before boarding his flight, Pochettino not only waved to his adoring fans, but took a photo with staff and players on the pitch in Cincinnati.

Recent findings suggest that 'It's impossible not to cry, but that is because we care about the people and the people care about us,' he told reporters. 'When that happens, it's normal to show your emotions, no? Because we are human. We are no robots.'.

Industry observers note that zeki Çelik was withdrawn from Türkiye's starting line-up in Bordeaux after feeling tightness in the same left thigh muscle he injured in October. With Pierre Kalulu already sidelined, Juventus face tests that could leave them without both main right-sided defenders for Venezia and Omonia.

Recent findings suggest that zeki Çelik’s international week ended before kick-off in Bordeaux. The Juventus full-back was named in Türkiye’s starting line-up for Sunday’s Nations League match against France. His left hamstring tightened up as he went through the warm-up. He was taken out of the matchday squad as a precaution. Barış Alper Yılmaz started in his place.

Sources indicate that an Emirhan Topçu own goal and a goal from Eli Junior Kroupi put France ahead. Abdülkerim Bardakcı scored a late reply for Türkiye. The result left France top of Nations League Group A1 with 13 points. They are through to the quarter-finals, which are due next March.

Çelik now returns to Turin for tests at J|Medical. Those results will decide how Juventus line up at the back after the international break.

In a recent development, the location is what worries Juventus. Çelik was substituted at half-time in the 2-2 Europa League draw with Rennes. His scans took place on the morning of Friday 23 October. He began a rehabilitation programme straight away and was expected back after the November break.

In a recent development, tuttosport counted him among Spalletti’s first returning players, alongside Vicario and Gatti. The paper placed the Bordeaux problem in the biceps femoris of his left thigh. That is the same area as the October injury.

Çelik had only just returned after weeks out. That is why the warm-up incident has raised fears of a relapse. No diagnosis has yet been confirmed.

Juventus were already without Pierre Kalulu. He picked up the injury in the game against Fiorentina. He began treatment and was withdrawn from the France squad. Sky Sport Italia expected him to be out for about three weeks. That would rule him out of both the Venezia and Omonia matches.

Sources indicate that if Çelik’s problem proves to be a relapse, Spalletti could be without both of his main right-sided defenders for those two games. The schedule offers little room for recovery. The Omonia match is the second of four games in 12 days.

It has been revealed that the league position adds pressure. After 11 rounds Juventus are seventh in Serie A with 18 points. Their record reads five wins, three draws and three defeats.

Venezia visit Turin first, at 12:30 on 22 November in round 12 of Serie A. Omonia then come to the Allianz Stadium at 21:00 on 26 November in the Europa League league phase.

By Saikat Mandal | 21 Nov 2026 15:08.

Two of the Premier League's most successful clubs renew their fierce rivalry on Sunday as Liverpool welcome Manchester United to Anfield for their first meeting of the season.

The Reds are navigating a period of transition under Andoni Iraola, but have made an encouraging start to the campaign, climbing to fourth in the Premier League table with 18 points.

Manchester United, meanwhile, have endured their worst start to a latest season, prompting the club hierarchy to part ways with Michael Carrick, who guided them into the Champions League places last term.

The Red Devils have wasted little time in appointing Mauricio Pochettino as his successor, but the Argentine faces a daunting introduction to the rivalry, having won just three of his 19 managerial meetings with Liverpool.

Here, Sports Mole provides everything you need to know about how to tune into the contest.

Liverpool vs Man Utd is one of two Premier League fixtures scheduled for Sunday, with the other seeing Hull City welcome Brighton & Hove Albion.

The eagerly anticipated clash at Anfield is scheduled to get underway at 4.30pm UK time, a prime Sunday afternoon slot that should allow supporters both in the stands and watching from around the world to savour one of English football's biggest rivalries.

Liverpool vs Man Utd will take place at Anfield, the 61,276-capacity stadium that has served as the spiritual home of the mighty Reds since 1892.

Anfield is the fifth-largest football stadium in England and has been the setting for countless memorable encounters between these fierce rivals, with its famous atmosphere often adding another layer of intensity.

Beyond football, the iconic venue also opens its doors to major musical events during the off-season, with global superstar Taylor Swift among the major-name artists to have performed there during her record-breaking Eras Tour.

Non-Sky customers can stream the contest through a NOW Day or cancel-anytime Month pass, while viewers in India can catch the action live on JioHotstar.

Liverpool and Man Utd's official X accounts are expected to share match snippets throughout the contest, while journalists covering the game may also post their own footage and updates.

After the final whistle, extended highlights should be available on both clubs' official YouTube channels, while viewers in the UK can catch the action again on BBC's Match of the Day 2.

Liverpool have an opportunity to cut the gap to Manchester City to just one point with victory on Sunday, giving them an added incentive to make home advantage count.

The Reds have endured an uncomfortable run against their fiercest rivals at Anfield, having failed to beat the Red Devils on home soil since their emphatic 7-0 triumph in March 2023, and Iraola will be desperate to put that unwanted sequence behind them by claiming all three points.

The likes of Bradley Barcola and Florian Wirtz will be eager to rise to the occasion and deliver on a stage of such magnitude, but Liverpool's overriding priority is to turn their home performances into consistent results and strengthen their position in the title race.

For Man Utd, the stakes are arguably even higher, with the visitors desperate to climb out of the relegation zone and give their troubled campaign some much-needed impetus.

Pochettino, meanwhile, will be keen to mark the beginning of his Man Utd tenure with a statement victory, although he could hardly have been handed a more demanding opening assignment; given the circumstances, even a hard-earned draw at Anfield would represent a respectable start to his reign.

Industry News: Observation of tunable superradiant frequency combs

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 17 min read (3423 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~17 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that cavity quantum electrodynamics1 with quantum emitters coupled to resonators provides a powerful platform for engineering light–matter interactions2,3 and exploring many-body phenomena4,5. In particular, superradiance6—arising from collective quantum interference among emitters—has been explored as a route to ultrastable continuous radiation7. However, engineering superradiance in the time domain to realize periodic pulsed sources or frequency combs remains largely unexplored. Here we investigate the non-equilibrium many-body dynamics of a driven spin ensemble coupled with an on-chip superconducting resonator and uncover a dynamical phase transition from continuous-wave to periodic pulsed superradiant emission. To quantitatively capture the observed dynamical phases, we introduce a driven-dissipative cavity-quantum electrodynamics model that elucidates how the periodic pulsed superradiant phase emerges from collective, periodically repeating spin dynamics stabilized by the interplay of coherence growth, disorder and dissipation. We also find that rare-earth ion spin systems with both optical and microwave transitions enable phase-synchronized, dual-rail superradiant frequency combs in both the microwave and the optical domains. Our results not only open newly introduced opportunities for atom-based frequency-comb sources and programmable superradiant generation, but establish a fundamental connection between periodic pulsed superradiance and the emergence of a continuous time crystal8,9,10 as a new non-equilibrium phase in driven open systems.

In a recent development, a, Detailed device schematic. A niobium film is patterned on a 500 μm thick 171Yb3+:YVO4 crystal. A 100 nm gold layer is evaporated on the back side, forming a weak optical Fabry-Pérot mode between the front and back chip reflections. b, Calibration of spin-cavity coupling strength. By optically pumping the population into the \(| \downarrow \rangle \) state, we probe the resonant spin-cavity coupling spectrum and its strength while avoiding superradiant effects. The blue data in the bottom subpanel correspond to the continuous-wave (CW) pump being off, while the black data are taken with a 400 μW continuous-wave pump. By fitting to a spin-cavity coupling model, we extract an ensemble coupling strength of \(\sqrt{N}g\approx 2\pi \times 1.1\) MHz, corresponding to a normalized coupling gnorm ≈ 0.6 < 1. The single-spin coupling, g = 2π × 10 Hz, and the effective ensemble size, N = 1010, are estimated from Comsol simulation and dopant concentration. c, Ensemble coupling strength, \(\sqrt{N}g\), as a function of pump power. We observe that the ensemble coupling strength increases with pump power, indicating a larger population in the microwave spin manifold.

Recent findings suggest that a, A pulsed, transient optical pumping scheme that drives 171Yb3+ spins into the \(| \uparrow \rangle \) state. The resulting inverted spin polarization is resonantly coupled to a microwave cavity, leading to a superradiant burst in the microwave domain. b, Example of a delayed superradiant burst. A 1 mW pump is applied for 50 μs, after which a microwave superradiant burst is observed with a delay time τd. The superradiant signal is normalized by its peak-to-peak amplitude. c and d, Burst delay times, τd, and burst width, τw, measured as a function of the optical pump detuning, Δpump, which controls the optical transition strength from \(| g\rangle \) to \(| \uparrow \rangle \). A symmetric dependence of τd and τw is observed, with shorter delay times and narrower widths near resonance. This behaviour is consistent with the expected scaling τd, τw ∝ 1/N, as the pump detuning effectively controls the ensemble size, N, in the microwave spin manifold. Data points represent mean values, with error bars indicating the standard deviation over 300 repeated measurements.

It has been revealed that a, Frequency-domain measurement of continuous-wave microwave superradiance, showing a much narrow linewidth of  ≈ 30 Hz. The inhomogeneously broadened ensemble line profile (dashed line) is overlaid for comparison. b, Dependence of the linewidth of continuous-wave superradiance on emission power, PMW. An inverse relationship between the linewidth and the emission power is observed, consistent with a noise-broadened Schawlow-Townes linewidth. The lower dashed line denotes the pump laser noise-limited bound. These results confirm that the disordered spin ensemble emits continuous-wave superradiance with a much narrower spectral linewidth. c, Continuous-wave superradiance emission frequency at different optical pump detunings. A linear correlation between the microwave emission frequency and optical pump detuning is observed, with a slope of  −1.23 kHz/MHz.

a, Four representative data traces under a 1 ms continuous optical pump. Random onset times of the emergent periodic pulsed phase are observed. b, Zoom-in of individual burst trains showing the distribution of burst onset times, {τk}, where k denotes the experimental repetition index. After an initial settling time, both the amplitudes, {Ak}, and the periodicity, T, become independent of k, indicating the establishment of a robust pulsed superradiance phase. c, Burst onset phases, defined as θk = 2π × τk/T (mod 2π), measured over 50 repetitions under identical experimental conditions. The phases are randomly distributed over 2π, demonstrating spontaneous breaking of continuous time-translation symmetry in the absence of any external timing reference.

In a recent development, a, Schematic of periodic pulsed superradiance, characterized by three parameters: the pulse-train periodicity T, the peak emission power Ppeak, and the average emission power \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\). b-d, show fits to the experimental data presented in Fig. 3 of the main text, where T, Ppeak, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\) exhibit good agreement with the expected scaling behaviours of T ∝ 1/N, Ppeak ∝ N2, and \({\overline{P}}_{{\rm{MW}}}\propto {N}^{2}\), respectively. Here, N is the effective number of spins in the microwave manifold, tuned via the optical pump detuning, Δpump. When sweeping Δpump, the optical pump power is fixed, corresponding to an excitation over an optical inhomogeneity Γop = 2π × 92 MHz in all three cases.

Recent findings suggest that a, Relative contributions of superradiance (blue) and stimulated emission (red) to the emission strength in the periodic superradiance phase. b, Comparison of emission patterns between the many-body case with N = 1010 atoms (blue) and the single-atom case with N = 1 (red). For a fair comparison, the total effective cavity coupling strength is fixed to \({g}_{{\rm{tot}}}=\sqrt{N}g=2\pi \times 1\,{\rm{MHz}}\) for both cases. c, Comparison of emission patterns in the presence (blue) and absence (red) of spin frequency inhomogeneity, i.e., disorder. All simulations are performed using experimental parameters corresponding to the periodic superradiance phase in Regime III.

a and b, show simultaneously recorded microwave periodic superradiance and transferred optical periodic superradiance, respectively, over a duration of up to 100 ms. c, Zoom-in windows near 1, 50, and 100 ms showing synchronized dual-rail emission patterns, maintaining persistent and robust pulse periodicity without decay.

Industry observers note that a, Microwave (blue) and optical (yellow) amplitudes, A(t), extracted from IQ detection as A(t) = ∣I(t) + iQ(t)∣. The I and Q signals, I(t) and Q(t), are measured continuously over 2 ms, capturing 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. The microwave and optical channels exhibit synchronized and reproducible temporal profiles. The grey shaded area indicates the noise floor determined from the optical signal, below which the phase extraction is not reliable. b, Normalized amplitude stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts. τ denotes the peak emission time, identified for each burst from the time-domain pulse train. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical normalized amplitudes, which are 0.009 and 0.05, respectively. c, Time-domain phase profiles, \(\phi (t)={\tan }^{-1}[Q(t)/I(t)]\), extracted from IQ detection. The microwave and optical pulse trains exhibit synchronized and reproducible phase profiles over time. Phase values in regions dominated by the optical-signal noise floor are greyed out, where large fluctuations are observed. The chirping behaviour during each pulse qualitatively follows the amplitude profile, which can be attributed to an effective Kerr nonlinearity induced intensity dependence. d, Phase stability over 30 consecutive superradiant bursts, zoomed in on the region above the noise floor. The error bars denote the standard deviations of the microwave and optical phase values, which are 0.03π and 0.11π, respectively. See Methods for details.

Chelsea suffer upcoming Moises Caicedo injury blow as Xabi Alonso forced into early Leeds change

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 15:43.
  • Chelsea have been dealt yet another injury blow concerning Moises Caicedo, who was forced off in the first half of Saturday's Premier League clash with Leeds United.
  • The 25-year-old was making his sixth start of the top-flight season at Stamford Bridge, joining Romeo Lavia in the centre of the park, but his race was run with just 22 minutes gone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Ben Knapton | 21 Nov 2026 15:24, Last updated: 21 Nov 2026 15:43.

Chelsea have been dealt yet another injury blow concerning Moises Caicedo, who was forced off in the first half of Saturday's Premier League clash with Leeds United.

The 25-year-old was making his sixth start of the top-flight season at Stamford Bridge, joining Romeo Lavia in the centre of the park, but his race was run with just 22 minutes gone.

Caicedo was involved in a heavy mid-air collision with James Justin early doors and was left in a heap on the ground, but he was ultimately able to carry on, albeit briefly.

The Ecuador international sat down on the turf just moments later and covered his face with his arm as he was attended to by medical staff, before hobbling off the field to be replaced by Jordan Henderson.

Caicedo appeared to be struggling with a back injury and was given an ice pack as he sat down on the bench, shortly before the Blues took the lead through Emmanuel Emegha.

The severity of Caicedo's latest concern is yet to be ascertained, and it may well be that the South American simply sustained a contact injury which will heal in a matter of days.

However, the midfielder's withdrawal prolonged a painful stop-start season, in which he has already missed six games across the Premier League and EFL Cup due to two separate injuries.

Industry observers note that caicedo sat out Chelsea's opening two games vs. Fulham and Luton Town owing to a knock, before picking up a calf problem just 14 minutes into his first appearance of the campaign against Brighton & Hove Albion.

The Blues faced Leeds (in the EFL Cup), Arsenal, Hull City and Brentford without Caicedo due to his new calf problem, since when he has been a mainstay in Alonso's midfield with the captain's armband.

The Ecuadorian is now an early doubt for next Friday's trip to Nottingham Forest, though, as well as Chelsea's London derby at home to Crystal Palace on December 2.

Caicedo's fitness struggles in the 2026-27 season are uncharacteristic, as the 25-year-old missed just two games through injury or illness in his first three campaigns at the club.

Both of those absences occurred in his debut 2023-24 campaign, in which he missed a 0-0 draw with Bournemouth because of a knock, and a 2-1 defeat to Wolverhampton Wanderers due to illness.

Caicedo navigated the entire 2024-25 season without picking up an injury, starting all 38 Premier League games and being omitted from several Conference League squads to enjoy a well-earned rest.

The midfielder then made another 50 appearances in the 2025-26 season, and his only notable absences were due to suspension rather than fitness problems.

Alonso is already missing Joao Pedro, Jamie Gittens, Maxence Lacroix, Jorrel Hato and Reece James, and none is expected to return before the end of the month.

Tech Report: Kane’s record-equalling cap was no different to his first

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

The 125th cap was no different to the first for Harry Kane, who has now been in the business of goal accumulation for so long that it is only at the landmark moments, that all of us are obliged to step back and take in the full scale of the work he has created.

Sources indicate that peter Shilton took 20 years to rack up his 125 caps, while for Kane it has been just 11 – and then there are the goals. Two more on Tuesday took him to 91 which means that only 12 other England players in history have more England caps than Kane has England goals. This unassuming man from Chingford, who looks like a mildly rebellious academic from the late 1950s, was at it again: the first-time strike, the back-post header. He has some misses across these 11 years, most infamously from the penalty spot against France at the Qatar World Cup almost four years ago, so, yes, there are some regrets too. But what sticks is the way he has taken his chances – again and again.

In a recent development, ONE-TOUCH BRILLIANCE! ✨ Anderson, Rogers and Kane combine beautifully to double England's lead 🏴󠁧󠁢󠁥󠁮󠁧󠁿 Cap No. 125, goal No. 90 for the skipper 👏 https://t.co/otMcxlXyps.

Following his debut goal in 2015 against Lithuania, Kane has missed just 27 of the 152 England games since. He has added to the total like a great Test batsman patiently moving the scoreboard along. There was a bad run without goals in 2020 and before that in 2018. He scored only five in his first 17 caps and then scored 14 in his next 10. Against a very mediocre Czech Republic team this was classic late-era Kane, picking his moments and taking those chances with the usual absence of nerves. He was even substituted before the end.

According to recent reports, hall ➡️ Kane! The Newcastle fullback swings in the corner and it's the England captain who rises highest to head home 💥 https://t.co/5EhAcNZUqm.

Afterwards at a Wembley press conference to mark the occasion, he invoked the cricket analogy himself on the question of scoring 100 England goals. “Being in the 90s, I try not to think about it too much, and it’s like I guess being a cricketer in the 90s. The more you think about the hundred… you don’t always get there.” There has still not been the elusive major trophy in the Kane England years but there has been success relative to the three decades that came before it. Semi-finals, finals – a good team if not a winning team.

At the centre of it has been a man around whom there has never been any scandal or, by the usual measure, much that might be described as spectacular. Rather it has been the scope of Kane’s career that is the most striking. The volume of the goals, of appearances, the capacity to be available – to play, to score – and the absolute quality of the player himself. He is determined to wring the very last drop out of his talent and usually refuses to acknowledge the prospect of the end, although there was a nod to it this time. “At some stage you know this opportunity isn’t going to be here,” he said. “I’m not going to be around forever, and I still hope that’s a long way away. But ultimately, of course, there’s times you’re tired or you’re injured, but I know I’ll miss it when it’s done. I try to always remind myself that and always try to make myself available.”.

Industry observers note that one expects that when the end comes it will not be as rancorous as the final exit of Cristiano Ronaldo from Portugal, a drama playing out elsewhere. At some point, Kane will take his leave and it is likely to be as unassuming as the rest of it. He will be back at Wembley, injury permitting, for cap No 126 next month against Croatia. He talks like a different person to the one he was even five years ago – with a confidence and certainty about his place in the world. As opposed to the younger Kane, who seemed to regard everything outside his goalscoring tunnel vision with a general sense of bemusement.

Recent findings suggest that “Availability,” he said, “is one of the biggest strengths you can have at this level for any coach.” He was keen to emphasise his “all-round leadership” too, “a lot of assets off the pitch”. He still measures himself in goals, of course, and perhaps there will be a Ballon d’Or too later this month – a prize that has eluded generations of England players before him who have won much more for their clubs than Kane has done. The good news for Kane is that his last England years will be spent in a very good England team – one which was on another level to its opposition on this occasion too.

Thomas Tuchel believes England have taken a step forward from their World Cup heartbreak over this international break and noted he was “honoured” to hear fans sing his name.

England finished their four Nations League games with a 3-0 win over Czech Republic, in which Harry Kane scored twice on his record-equalling 125th appearance.

It meant that Tuchel’s team have won three and lost one, against Spain, of their four games since the World Cup, after which the England head coach was heavily criticised for the semi-final defeat to Argentina.

Tuchel seems to have won the forgiveness of some England supporters, who sang his name at the start and the end of Tuesday’s game.

Industry observers note that “It means a lot,” Tuchel remarked. “It’s amazing to have a song. It’s the biggest honour. And I’m very happy and very honoured. They can be sure that I will give my absolute best to make our team win and play well.”.

Asked if he sensed a change in mood around his England team since the fall-out from the World Cup, Tuchel stated: “I do and I think it’s necessary to move on. I think I can only repeat that we didn’t go out in the group stage. Sometimes it feels like that and we didn’t. As I said, our aim was always to progress, move forward and improve.”.

Tuchel snapped back at a reporter who questioned why he felt it necessary to repeat that England had not gone out in the group stage of the World Cup, claiming the criticism had felt a “little bit” too harsh.

In a recent development, but on whether England have shown they are a step ahead of where the team were at the World Cup during this international camp, Tuchel was far more positive and replied: “Of course and that’s what we have to do. That is our goal to constantly improve and develop.

“We had these experiences together and we had a big tournament together, and it was very positive. It’s necessary to move forward and improve, especially in sports. This is what we’re trying to do.

Industry observers note that “We adjusted some details in our structure and we didn’t compromise on the effort and the intensity, and on the togetherness of the team. Recent findings suggest that sparkling in Como, Nico Paz chose to permanently join the Italian club, to which he was loaned last season, instead of staying at Real Madrid. A profitable choice since the 22-year-old attacking midfielder shines under the orders of Cesc Fàbregas and has even become international with Argentina who see him as the successor to Lionel Messi. His performances with Como have not gone unnoticed by Madrid, since Real Madrid seem inclined to activate his buyout clause estimated at 80 million euros, confirms COPE.

According to recent reports, according to the Iberian media, the club chaired by Florentino Pérez wishes to repatriate its former player, trained at La Fábrica. As a reminder, this clause is only valid for next summer. Last summer, Como paid 60 million euros to buy him from Madrid. Since then, he has played 14 matches for a total of eight goals and six assists, in all competitions, and has confirmed his upcoming acquired status.

Inside the 'uncomfortable' world of football documentaries: The shocking 'lack of respect' shown to managers, how Pep Guardiola learned to love the cameras - and why Mauricio Pochettino's appointment is bad news for Amazon's crew at Carrington

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.
  • Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JACK GAUGHAN and NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026 | Updated: 21:00 EST, 18 November 2026.

Paul Scholes and Phil Neville took charge of the Salford City team for one afternoon only, celebrity juxtaposed with the surroundings of a Northern Premier League Division One North fixture in a bracing January cold, played out before a few hundred supporters.

It has been revealed that the club’s new managers, a double act from nearby Ramsbottom United, stood behind the goal studying the Salford squad. Neville approached them at full time, asking if they’d like to say a few words inside the dressing room – or more accurately, portacabin – by way of introduction.

In a recent development, ‘It was dark at full time,’ co-manager Anthony Johnson recalls. ‘I’m not exaggerating the point, I opened the door and there were these cameras, these lights on. Nobody told us about a documentary.

'The lights literally came on and I went, “S***, I’m under the spotlight here”. There was no training, nobody sits you down to tell you how it works.’.

First airing in a primetime slot on BBC One, Salford’s Class of ’92 docuseries was hooked on the Manchester United legends owning the club but swiftly became a show about the shouty personalities of Johnson and his partner, Bernard Morley, charting three promotions through non-League from 2015.

Recent findings suggest that salford are the smallest club ever to be the focus of this form of storytelling. Now, such documentaries are a popular vehicle for the country's elite.

Co-managers Anthony Johnson (left) and Bernard Morley became the accidental stars of a BBC documentary about the Class of 92's ownership of Salford City.

The celebrity of (from left) Paul Scholes, Nicky Butt, Ryan Giggs and Phil Neville was juxtaposed with Salford's humble facilities on the series.

The Amazon cameras were in for Manchester City’s title-winning campaign in 2018 and also collaborated with the club to document the end of Pep Guardiola’s reign.

In a recent development, they are across town this year, right in the middle of United’s worst start to a season since the 1980s. Amid the infighting, public rows, Michael Carrick’s sacking and Mauricio Pochettino’s appointment, the streaming service should emerge as the real victors of what has been an inconceivably dismal three months at Old Trafford.

The sight of a camera crew scuttling out of a press conference with Carrick weeks before he was relieved of his duties, boom mic hovering, painted a neat picture of the additional stress that can be placed upon managers when the pound signs prove too large for executives to ignore.

It has been revealed that ‘You can’t be yourself,’ claims Simon Grayson, Sunderland manager at the start of their infamous Netflix drama Sunderland 'Til I Die, with part one culminating in relegation from the Championship in the 2017-18 season. ‘You never forgot the cameras are there.’.

According to recent reports, like Johnson, Grayson had been unaware of the planned documentary. David Moyes rejected the idea the year before when he was Sunderland boss, just as Ruben Amorim did at United in 2025.

Recent findings suggest that grayson didn’t grant Netflix access to ‘the inner sanctum’ and provided them footage of training remotely. Wrexham boss Phil Parkinson has had the power to dictate where and when crews can film across their 57 episodes of Welcome to Wrexham.

Sources indicate that ‘I’m a private person,’ Grayson adds. ‘I don’t like people seeing what I’m doing. There were times when they actually tried to overstep the mark... you’d limit them to where the cameras would be.

It has been revealed that 'Even the players would say they were apprehensive and felt it was a bit intrusive. Aiden McGeady noted that he felt really uncomfortable doing it, as the rest of the dressing room did.’.

Vincent Kompany didn't like the way he was portrayed as a hot-head in a documentary during his time at Burnley.

Pep Guardiola relaxed his attitude towards the film-makers covering Man City when they learned where to position themselves in his dressing room without acting as a distraction.

Intriguingly, Guardiola embraced the cameras – but only eventually, initially insisting that filming could not resemble a circus. There was a scarcity of dressing room footage in Amazon’s 2018 edition. Only the notorious tirade at his players during half-time of a tempestuous FA Cup defeat at Wigan made it but that changed when City embedded their own production staff.

Sources say a relaxing of rules took time, around 12 months, as camera operators learned where to stand without acting as a distraction or finding themselves physically in the way.

City have been part of five documentaries in six years now, with Guardiola so enamoured by the producers that they became part of the backroom staff – even acting as auxiliary kit men on away days. He sent personal audio messages of thanks when he bid farewell last May.

He utilised them to create montages for pre-match speeches and leant on them to film players in slow motion to watch the gait of a player recovering from injury. That comes from the cameras being part of the furniture.

Critics will argue an in-house production is to the detriment of the eventual sanitised product, although City will point to Guardiola’s emotional breakdowns in A Beautiful Obsession – the story of his final season at City – as being raw and uncut.

The format is now moving towards in-season docs (regular episodes being available during a season rather than the whole show coming out at the end). This mirrors success stories in NFL and A Beautiful Obsession co-director John De Caux believes full-season pieces are ‘slightly on the wane’.

‘There were changes (in camera staff) all the time,’ Johnson indicates, reflecting on Salford’s annual series while he was in charge. ‘We were losing at half-time in one game… I make no apologies for this but I came in and went, “Move out of the f***ing way”. In previous seasons, they’d know not to be in that position.

Sources indicate that ‘You're having the same conversations again. It was like, "Hang on a minute. I've had this conversation before". The previous people knew about it. They have the footage from earlier seasons – so do your homework, like we all do with our jobs. It almost felt like a bit of a lack of respect at times.’.

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for an eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise cameras were rolling.

Former Sunderland boss Simon Grayson was unaware of their planned Netflix documentary and didn't grant the producers access to his inner sanctum.

These are the challenges that Amazon face with United, somehow attempting to earn trust or forging relationships in a matter of months before they pack up and leave. The film crew will be seen as outsiders.

There is intrigue within the industry as to exactly how granular Amazon can go amid the United chaos and whether they use fly-on-the-wall cameras, as was the case with Arsenal (in 2021–22) and Tottenham (in 2019-20).

The Spurs All or Nothing is memorable for that eye-popping scene between Danny Rose and Jose Mourinho, when the left back didn’t realise the cameras were rolling.

Recent findings suggest that unlike Mourinho, Pochettino – his predecessor, sacked in November 2019 – had banned them from his office. He was never keen on the idea of the documentary and hardly features in the series, his dismissal coming early in Episode One – a sign perhaps that the film-makers got little out of him.

It will be fascinating to see if they gain access to his inner sanctum at United.

The club have had to double their media commitments this season as a result of the streaming deal, although they have been reluctant to organise sitdown interviews with players, telling Amazon that they must establish their own rapport for those.

In a recent development, some clubs have been known to give their content away for free, with Sky Sports taking two seasons of Mission to Burnley without paying. The driving force behind those moves is to promote brands. Under Alan Pace’s premiership, Burnley are staring at potential relegation to League One.

Vincent Kompany, then the Burnley manager, is understood to have been vexed at his portrayal as a hot-headed screamer. Brendan Rodgers cannot have been overly pleased with Being: Liverpool, which ended in public ridicule and comparisons to David Brent. Players at other clubs have confided that they hid from cameras.

‘You can’t be yourself, you never forget the cameras are there,’ says Grayson of his season alongside the makers of Sunderland 'Til I Die.

Salford's co-manager Anthony Johnson gives his players a dressing down in the BBC documentary.

Joey Barton, meanwhile, is still waiting for his moment – and may be for some time. Fleetwood Town commissioned their own team to chart his start in management and streaming giants Dazn purchased the rights.

It was so close to being aired that Fleetwood held a premiere at Highbury Stadium for 100 supporters including the local mayor, only for one of Barton’s brushes with law enforcement in the intervening days to suspend the broadcast. Prolonged legal proceedings meant the idea was canned and Dazn’s licencing period expired.

According to recent reports, it was later resurrected, focusing in part on then Fleetwood owner Andy Pilley’s fraud trial – a crew followed him into court on day one – but was then shelved when a guilty verdict was handed down. Cameras are following clubs up and down the EFL from Birmingham to Cambridge via Sheffield Wednesday.

Grayson, for his part, refused to share his drive home from training with the crew and now admits that the ultimately unfavourable edit may have been a result of him not giving the production company what they wanted.

‘I did a presentation with the players with a flip chart and everybody thought it was an hour before kick-off of a league game,’ he claims. ‘It was actually done at 11:30am before a pre-season game!

'That’s why I let them film it, because it was a pre-season game, and it had no real meaning. But they presented it in the doc as if it was before the first game of the season.

Sources indicate that 'Part of the severance when I was sacked was that I still needed to do some work for them. I did three different (choreographed) interviews in a London hotel with different shirts on after I’d been sacked, done as if they were filmed at the time.

‘People said, “You didn’t come across that passionate about the club when you were talking about it”. Well, why would you when you were filming in November after you’d already been sacked? We were talking about deadline day in one of them. I’d already done something on that in August.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I think they had sympathy with me, but also if they’d had more sympathy, they wouldn’t have even asked me to do it. I’ve spoken to managers since and they’ve gone, “F***ing hell, you did well to put up with that".'.

Grayson only ever watched four episodes back and has heard his successor, Chris Coleman, was also dealt a raw deal.

Fabian Delph leads a Manchester City inquest during an FA Cup defeat at Wigan - the only scene from the dressing room that made it into Amazon's documentary on the 2017-18 season.

In a recent development, mauricio Pochettino banned cameras from his office in his final days at Tottenham. Will he do the same at Manchester United?

Sources indicate that by his own admission, Johnson enjoyed the process more than Grayson did. One ex-Salford player claimed that nothing was really cut from the show other than a fight on a team-bonding night out. It was authentic, no-holds barred.

Until the end of Johnson and Morley, that is.

‘We won the league and we ended up getting sacked anyway,’ Johnson indicates. ‘We went to meet Gary (Neville) and the board. We went upstairs in Hotel Football and a cameraman followed us. Obviously they knew what was going on. When we got to the room for the meeting, they wouldn't let the camera in.

‘I'm actually smiling thinking about it. The documentary followed me and Bern everywhere, eating food or whatever, and then when the day comes to sack us, they didn't want the camera in the room!

‘The conversation was fine in the room itself but I think the perception from the outside world looking in would've been: "What the f*** is that all about?”’.

Juventus have sold out Sunday's Serie A home game against Venezia despite a long injury list. Strong early sales for the Europa League visit of Omonia Nicosia keep the club in line for another strong European crowd.

Juventus go into Sunday’s home game against Venezia still short of players. Several remain unavailable for Sunday’s 12:30 kick-off. Edon Zhegrova has trained with the group and is considered available. Celik, Cambiaso, Nico Gonzalez and Kalulu remain out, Sport Mediaset reported. For Spalletti, a full home crowd arrives in the middle of a busy run of games.

In a recent development, general sale for the fixture opened at 3pm on Tuesday 6 October. Supporters living in the province of Venezia could buy only if they held an active Juventus Card. The fixture belongs to the 2026-27 Serie A Enilive season.

Industry observers note that this season every Juventus match ticket is digital. Each one is managed through the Allianz Stadium App.

Sources indicate that season-ticket holders who cannot attend can list their seat on resale.juventus.com. The club, not the seller, sets the resale price. A few of those listings are now all that remains for supporters who missed the general sale, ANSA reported.

The season-ticket terms also reward turning up. To keep first refusal on a 2027-28 season ticket, a holder must use the seat for at least 70 per cent of matches. That means at least 13 of the 19 league games.

Industry observers note that the Europa League has drawn big numbers to Turin this season. Against NEC, 39,308 match tickets were sold, with away fans counted separately. No away figure was released for the Rennes visit, but that section was full.

Sources indicate that the Rennes game finished 2-2 on 22 October. Juventus needed a second-half Woltemade penalty to draw after trailing 2-1.

Omonia Nicosia are next. Bookings for the Cypriot club’s visit still trail the two earlier European crowds.

According to recent reports, juventus have set strict conditions for the fixture. Supporters of Cypriot nationality may buy tickets only for the away section. The club has warned that breaking UEFA rules can lead to cancelled tickets and refused entry.

According to recent reports, taken together, the figures are consistent with a home support that keeps buying despite the injury list. The weekend league fixture will be followed by a European night that is already well on its way to another large crowd.

Juventus host Omonia Nicosia in the Europa League on 26 November.

In a recent development, virgil van Dijk does not seem particularly worried about his future at Liverpool. While his contract with the Reds expires next June, the 35-year-old Dutch defender has still not made a decision on the rest of his career. Discussions with club management are expected in the coming weeks and months, but the captain prefers to remain focused on the current season. “I want to keep playing and doing what I do, so we’ll see what the season brings.”he explained.

Before adding: “If this continues, so much the better. Otherwise, I’ll go elsewhere. There’s nothing to report at the moment, but that doesn’t mean I’m panicking. Arriving at the end of his previous contract in June 2025, the Dutchman finally extended it for two seasons in April of the same year. This time, no decision has yet been made regarding his future, while Liverpool may have to consider the succession of their captain.

Mykhailo Mudryk has blamed his stint with the Ukrainian national team for the failed doping test which cost him two years of his career and revealed how fighting his case personally cost him millions of pounds.

The Chelsea winger, who is now on loan with Tottenham Hotspur, has opened up for the first time since he returned to football in the summer when his suspension was suddenly lifted.

According to recent reports, it was in a two-hour interview with Ukrainian journalist Dmitry Gordon via his YouTube channel. While the title of the video mentions ‘suicidal thoughts’, Mudryk clarifies during the conversation that he did not consider committing suicide despite being in a dark place. ‘Kill myself – no, that’s not a way out,’ he said when asked that question.

But he did discuss how Chelsea broke the news of his failed test to him, whether they helped their £89million signing from Shakhtar Donetsk during his ban, his belief that the drug meldonium entered his system while he was in Ukraine, and why he is now with Tottenham. He further claimed that he has faced threats from gangsters, and admitted his dream is to someday win the Ballon d’Or.

It has been revealed that on the Ukrainian national team and their federation, the Ukrainian Association of Football, Mudryk said: ‘I’ll be honest, it pretended to help. But in reality, there was no help. They created more problems than they solved. Especially when we needed help the most, they turned their backs on us.

'I just would like, for the future, everyone to understand that you can only rely on yourself.'.

Mykhailo Mudryk has spoken publicly for the first time about the doping case that cost him two years of his career.

Mudryk has criticised the Ukrainian Association of Football over their support during his case.

Daily Mail Sport contacted the Ukrainian Association of Football for comment.

It has been revealed that continuing, Mudryk said: ‘The UAF is afraid of being left to blame in this situation, and afraid of the criticism or whatever else might come raining down. Distancing themselves from their own player, not helping, pretending to help, and in the end, first they drag the case out for months without really helping the case in the end. But at least the UAF isn’t to blame.’.

According to recent reports, mudryk was handed an initial four-year ban after being charged by the Football Association for failing a doping test, with his last appearance prior to that coming in November 2024 in the Conference League away at Heidenheim. He scored in that 2-0 win for Chelsea. He was able to return when a seismic resolution was struck after changes to the 'scientific reporting standards'. Mudryk appeared for Chelsea during their pre-season tour before joining Tottenham on loan.

On how and why he failed his test, Mudryk mentioned: ‘I had never heard of a drug like meldonium, never seen it, never come across it in my life. I only learned about it when they told me the news. I definitely have ideas. It’s a drug you can only get in Eastern Europe.

Industry observers note that ‘This drug could only have got into my body where I was, and that’s Ukraine. There are no such drugs in England. It supposedly stimulates your heart and helps you, as far as I understand, handle physical load better.

It has been revealed that ‘I was at home and Chelsea’s management came to see me and they said we needed to talk. Then they say you’ve returned a positive doping test and now you’re facing a ban.

‘You can’t believe it’s true. You can’t believe this is happening to you. If I’d ever taken anything anywhere, I’d have understood that this conversation might happen one day.

‘At least I’d have understood it was possible. But when you spend a huge pile of money on watching your diet, on a nutritionist, on a chef. When you spend that much money every year on all these things, that’s the last thing you expect. Because it speaks for itself: that you take things very seriously, like nutrition, everything that goes into your body, you watch it very closely.

It has been revealed that ‘Otherwise there’d be no need to spend money on it, because you could manage without it. They tell you this news, and you sit there, and you kind of listen to them but don’t hear them.

Mudryk returned to action when his ban was lifted in August, with the winger revealing Xabi Alonso told him to get game time and that he was 'counting on him'.

The Ukrainian joined Tottenham on loan but has seen injury restrict his involvement to date.

‘At some point you just go into a trance. It feels like you’re falling in a dream off a skyscraper. You’re flying down, you feel yourself flying down, and only in a dream do you wake up when you hit the ground, but in real life you don’t wake up, you just keep falling. It hits you very hard mentally. At that moment the tears came later.’.

According to recent reports, mudryk revealed how ‘the figure is in the millions’ when asked about the lawyers fees which were needed to fight his case. He confirmed he paid for that himself, along with the personal trainers and massage therapists he used to maintain his fitness while suspended. However, Mudryk did add that Chelsea continued to pay his salary during his time out of football.

Sources indicate that on joining Tottenham and being reunited with Roberto De Zerbi, who formerly managed him at Shakhtar Donetsk, Mudryk said: ‘It’s a perfectly logical decision. The club (Chelsea) has a new coach (Xabi Alonso), he sees football his own way. He sees the players he needs for that football. He came up and told me straight to my face: “You’d better go and play, get some game time, and then come back to Chelsea. I’m counting on you.”’ On De Zerbi, he added: ‘We met and he says: “Are you happy? Come on, we’ve still got a lot of work to do together.”’.

Mudryk added how difficult it was after switching to England and, along with encountering issues with his former representatives who encouraged him to move to Chelsea rather than Arsenal, he noted: 'They give you ultimatums, you know. That’s how it is.’.

It’s the 56-year-old’s second attempt at Serie A after coaching Cremonese for half a season in 2022-23. He didn’t manage a single win then, so you can definitely say that the performance so far has been great revenge for him.

It has been revealed that it doesn’t mean that they sit back, though. In fact, it has been the opposite as they are the highest-pressing team in the league. The strategy thus seems to be to force mistakes out of the opponents, while also making sure that they are direct in possession.

They aren’t exactly massive-name players, so a lot of them are having their breakout seasons.

Moving on to actual team news, the situation up front is not ideal for Frosinone as their top scorer, the aforementioned Antonio Raimondo, is out injured. Birigilea, who is on two goals, is set to replace him in the No.9 position.

The Milan academy product Sebastiano Desplanches, who left the club four years ago, will be on the bench. He’s yet to make an appearance this season, with Alvini preferring Lorenzo Palmisani instead.

Predicted Frosinone XI (4-2-3-1): Palmisani; Oyono, Calvani, Monterisi, Terzic; Calo, Masini; Ghedjemis; Schmid, Kvernadze; Birigilea.
